beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used three different mugs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning this piano. Please leave the keys alone while I listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking the sticky ones so you can fix those too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Mark them with these little stickers. Silently, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. Shall I peel them off so you can play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One at a time. After I reach each key. We've nearly invented a system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice acceptance speech. I taught you to project, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to order pizza when I was eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And tonight an auditorium heard you. Progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally applying my lesson about not asking for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely portrait. You're finally getting the shadows I tried to teach you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My new teacher told me to stop mixing everything with black.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're ready to move beyond my introductory method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She made me throw out your paint set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You used to be far too sentimental. I was beginning to worry I'd never get you past that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only the caretaker. Plan whatever concert you like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll start at eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I unlock the hall at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we have a key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Submit your preferred concert time to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't put me on the committee. I only send the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've voted to invite the whole street.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How lovely. I'll send them to the six people I have addresses for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give you the full address list tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Just mark which six you'd most like me to find stamps for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations, Mayor Pudding Pants. Shall I sit with your mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't use that nickname at my inauguration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Mayor Pudding. She'll know who I mean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just Martin. The microphones are already on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Martin! Come and sit by your mum. I'll move her handbag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice corner office, Ben. Do I still have to climb through your window?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the director now. My assistant lets people in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Your mum used to do that, unless you were grounded.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sign the visitor book as a business contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does lending you my homework count? It certainly kept you in business.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You thanked 'transport' in your award speech. I drove you to that audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Let me buy you dinner to say thank you properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Somewhere with a good view of our award, I hope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put a photo of you beside it. Will that do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the one of us in the car. People should see how the award got there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your bakery looks wonderful. Where's my founder's discount?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lent me a mixing bowl. I've returned it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bowl came back. My contribution is still in every cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Have a free slice as a thank-you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every morning? Lovely. I'll bring the bowl back so you don't fall behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your lunch and labelled your umbrella. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working from home today. You can leave it to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put your lunch in the fridge. Apparently I need your work calendar too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll share it with you. Tomorrow says lunch out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll book you a table, then. Now I have to ring and check they have somewhere for your umbrella.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cleaned the kitchen while you slept. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to clean it at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And leave me knowing it was dirty until nine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Next time, wake me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now I'm responsible for your alarm too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded twelve towels. How many have you done?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not racing. I'm washing them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Different event. Convenient choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can win towel folding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not by concession. Fold one properly and make it count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your tomato's impressive. Mine weighs two grams more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're making a salad.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's keep the winning tomato separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already chopped it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. We'll compete by number of pieces.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you check my resignation letter? Just the spelling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spelling's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And resigning? Does that word suit me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask your manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask? I'd trust the answer more in your voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come into the dentist's with me. You always remember the instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll write them down. I can wait outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You should check his handwriting. Yours is the only one I never misread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll copy the note for you afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you do it as he talks? I don't want to spend the appointment misunderstanding him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put out the blue cups. So we're doing this again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the only clean ones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They were the only clean ones last time, too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wash the red ones. You choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Last time I chose, you remembered that part very clearly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting choice of song for our first road trip since the incident.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the traffic report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And they're mentioning that roundabout very casually.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can take another road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said before we needed another car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pastry is beautiful. I've copied the lattice, with one extra strip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those gaps let the steam out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's clever. I'll leave even more room for steam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. I press the edge with a fork. Here, use mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Have you got a fork with more prongs?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You make public speaking look effortless. I practised your shrug all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just be yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. My version of your shrug has more range.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a competition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That sounds so confident. I'm using that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'Lightning' on my retirement cake. That's what the band called me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake says Graham.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Graham worked in accounts. Lightning had a smoke machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small family party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then get a small smoke machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm keeping the motorcycle jacket on for the school run.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You came on a folding bicycle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same wind. Same man.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then help Sophie open her lunchbox. The catch is stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Roadside assistance. Stand back. I still know my way around a stubborn machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does the new receptionist have a key? I open this office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could take a day off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And let the door forget me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a spare key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep it safe. Spares are my department too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An electric mixer? I thought making your birthday cake was my job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It'll do the mixing. You can still choose the recipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're doing Mum's cake. She taught me the amounts by feel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write them down as you go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'a handful of flour.' My handful, obviously. You'll need me for that bit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered you the mild curry. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted the hot one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's exactly the impulse I'm protecting you from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've told the waiter not to believe you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I booked your quiet holiday instead of the climbing trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I love climbing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You love surviving it. I've kept that part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cancel the booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No refunds. Sometimes caring requires a deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought this blue shirt for the party. Don't worry, I'm not asking you to choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bit formal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll roll the sleeves up. I was going to anyway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's better. You look ready to do the washing-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll roll one down. I was aiming for someone who might help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm painting Independence on the boat. You're welcome to watch; the name's settled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a lot of letters to paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Indie, then. Cleaner lines.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the full name. I was offering to paint half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Independence, then. I was only shortening it to save you work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you help me fill the shelf I built? Start with that enormous atlas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fits. I'll put the rest of the books beside it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait a moment. Look how little the shelf bends. Even under an atlas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's solid. Shall I cover the brackets with the trailing plant?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we trim it first? I'd hate the real leaves to hide the ones I carved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my marathon medal beside the kettle. Accidentally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's blocking the tea bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A difficult obstacle. Much like mile twenty-three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Congratulations on the marathon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, you noticed? I haven't shown you the split times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please leave your sandwich wrapped. The picnic begins with three taps on the basket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The basket's in the car. Sam's driven off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we wait. This is a picnic, not people eating near each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll phone Sam. He can tap the basket for us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on speaker. No one unwraps anything until we hear the third tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please stand for the opening of the office fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only want my yoghurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We acknowledge the light before approaching the shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bulb's broken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today we open it in remembrance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a drop of water beside the kettle. We need an evacuation route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've identified the source. Stop producing water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the cloth? The threat has changed location.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That chair squeaked. Keep your weight exactly where it is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. It just needs oil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I'm planning an evacuation. You're adding a fire risk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll get off the chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not suddenly. That's your whole weight landing on the floor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The power's out! Our candle collection finally gets its premiere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't own candles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A shopping trip with a purpose!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shops have no power either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. The whole town's joining in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our flight's cancelled. We've been given a bonus airport day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hotel will only give us credit for another stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. We've already started paying for our next holiday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only valid on weekdays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. They're making sure we take time off work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's agreed to speak at our meeting. Can you give it five minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only speaks at midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Record it. We'll play it after the finance report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last night it predicted everyone leaving during the finance report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it before finance. I'd like someone left to hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Does its fire heat the water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. You won't need the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Great. It can have the money we save on gas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only accepts payment in gold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could it accept an annual payment? I don't think a month's gas makes a whole coin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody moves out until I find the paperclip from my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The removal van is charging by the hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the driver help look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can have the building. I want the paperclip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You changed 'regards' to 'best regards' in my email.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also got us the contract.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can discuss that after removing 'best.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a correction. Shall I withdraw the whole email?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just withdraw 'best.' I don't want them thinking I've withdrawn my regards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two red buses and now your red scarf. We're meant to paint the front door red.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me this scarf at Christmas.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've been part of it for months without knowing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbour's asking to borrow our paintbrush.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's been sent to do the painting. Tell him the door will be ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three of us, and the lift stops at three. Someone on this floor needs our help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are four of us. You missed the courier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's the guide. Ask him which door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's going to five. He's delivering a replacement kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three was where we met our guide. We're going to five; someone needs company for tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered everyone's sandwiches. We saved six minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm vegetarian.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already removed your ham. Seven minutes saved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I choose next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could, but I've ordered next time too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Chairs face the window. I've moved them while you were deciding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The speaker's at the other end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then moving the speaker is quicker than moving twelve chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already speaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then everyone turns their own chair. Twelve jobs at once. I'll count you in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm covering reception until two. Sign here and I'll send you up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The form asks for a visitor badge number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. We'll issue your badge before we finish the form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can wait for the receptionist to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No waiting. Open those drawers with me. You check left; I'll check right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: While Miss Bell's out, I'm taking the register. Names, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've got yesterday's list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll confirm the regulars first. Start at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got today's list. Shall I take over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it here. Keep yesterday's open; I'll call for comparisons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those towels need folding with the seams inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody sees them in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. That's why I'm qualified to stack them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I close the cupboard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you level the third towel. Doors don't correct technique.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave a finger's width between those mugs in the dishwasher.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've done that. They aren't touching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the same finger. You've measured one gap with your thumb.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the middle mug out. Plenty of space now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now centre the other two. You'd never leave gaps like that in a proper hotel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my usual table at this café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only opened today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, much fresher since my last visit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What would you like?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My usual. Let's see whether you've changed that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first night at the club? I'll show you the shortcut to the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the cleaner's cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've moved it again. We used to come this way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says it's upstairs. I'll show you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've restored the original route. You lead; I'll give you the history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me demonstrate how to tie that parcel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already tied it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Untie it. Learning begins with observation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's going to be opened anyway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay for my lesson on receiving a parcel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you make tea, watch my wrist with the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made tea for twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll appreciate the advanced pour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished the tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now make one under supervision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to open the supply cupboard. Which project is this for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We just need batteries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll need to know which drawer to authorise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll buy some.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I have the petty-cash key too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the room bookings. When do you want your meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's empty now. Can we start?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll tell you when the next group needs it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I photograph the list? Then we won't have to bother you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No bother. I'll bring it round when you need to stop. Just concentrate on your meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your chipped mug, my ugly mug. I'll wash; you dry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a dishwasher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. You load your side; I'll load mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's only one mug rack.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yours on the left, then. Pass me mine when it's done. We always put them away together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two knocks on your window. Ready for our usual walk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working from home now. Text first; I might be on a call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll text 'knock knock.' Same signal. I'll get your walking boots.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only got ten minutes at lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then straight to our usual bench. I'll bring the sandwiches. Your end, my end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll watch your dog tonight. That settles your fixing my sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He just sleeps. Your sink took three hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave him tomorrow too, then. Two nights for the awkward pipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave dinner for you. There's lasagne in the fridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't feed me. I'm trying to get even. If you cook as well, I'll have to take him on holiday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you water my plants? I covered your shift in March.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was one afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And these are only six small plants.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is a tree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shift included overtime.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've reminded you about the dentist tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in my calendar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll remind you to check the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sends alerts, but my phone has to stay in my locker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll remind you at lunch. And remind me to eat mine—no, I'll put that on my list too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bin day tomorrow. I've written it on your breakfast banana.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't always eat breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll put another reminder on the coffee machine. Apparently I track breakfast now too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll set a phone alarm. You can stop leaving notes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll leave one by your charger reminding you what the alarm means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the heavier shopping bag. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll carry both bags upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put everything away. Carrying gets points, but remembering where things go gets double.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it away too. You sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. I'll count how many times you ask me which cupboard. Those go in my column.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I arrived ten minutes early to help set up. That's ten in my column.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed an hour late yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Evenings count differently. Mine required getting out of bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You live upstairs. I caught the six o'clock bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you were already up. I interrupted actual sleep. We need a separate column for sacrifice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which counter takes these forms? Just checking they've not moved it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's been counter three for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wait. We need a queue ticket before we go over there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Which button gives us counter three? I'm checking they've labelled it sensibly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're opening the allotment shed. Which key do you usually use? I have my own method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The red one. Lift the handle first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I lift first too. Which way do you turn it afterwards? Comparing methods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Left. Here, I'll open it; we need the watering cans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go ahead. I'll check your sequence against mine. Slowly, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a sock on the stairs. We've reached this chapter again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dropped it just now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And last month 'just now' lasted three days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pick it up. Could you hold my tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm holding your tea again. Last month I ended up carrying the laundry too. Give me the basket; we're apparently at that bit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five minutes late for our anniversary dinner. We're doing last year again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bus broke down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last year it was a puncture. Dinner always starts with a transport report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I walked the last mile. I even brought your flowers on foot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flowers again. Shall I find last year's vase, or are we pretending this is a new apology?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Must be nice, cooking dinner in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I chop tomorrow's vegetables while tonight's dinner cooks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass me tomorrow's carrots, then. Lovely having a whole spare evening inside this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take half home. Tomorrow you only have to tip them in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the tub too. Apparently effortless people already have containers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered every birthday. Must be nice having that sort of time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I use phone reminders. Here, I'll send you the calendar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll import it. Some of us remember people because we care.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's also a reminder to buy the cards a week ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Turn that on too. Mum calls you thoughtful for obeying your phone. Don't tell her you've sent me this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We used to arrange dinner by saying 'dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we check six calendars. Thursday at seven works.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down. We used to manage six people with one shout up the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make it a standing booking. Then nobody has to check again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. A permanent reservation to recreate dropping in. We used to get that for knocking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our old shopping list just said bread, milk, eggs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we need oat milk for Jo and lactose-free for Dad.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write both. Milk used to take one line, and we all knew whose it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Save the list on your phone. We can reuse it every week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me save it, then. We used to finish the list before needing help with it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I get a lift? Only if it isn't trouble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll move my coat off the passenger seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't move it for me. I'll sit in the back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's full of shopping. Hold the coat; I'll turn the heating down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't change it. I'll keep the coat on my lap. If I get hot, I can get out and walk the rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I have another fork? Sorry, this one's bent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll get one from the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please sit down. I shouldn't have made you get up during dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm getting the pudding anyway. It isn't an extra trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then just bring pudding. I've already got a spoon. I'll save the peas for another time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed lunches for your first week at college.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My room doesn't have a fridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll drop one off every morning. I've labelled the days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lunch is included in my fees. I'm meeting my flatmates there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many flatmates? I'll pack theirs too. You can all meet me outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this raincoat to the picnic. I checked the forecast all week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny, and my bag's full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear it, then. I didn't spend seven mornings checking so you'd have nothing ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll be boiling. I could sit on it if the grass is wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll pack a water bottle. We can dampen a patch if necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've swept your kitchen. Anything else before I go?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just sit down. You're my guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair could use a polish first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I invited you for company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll talk while I polish. Two reasons to invite me again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've organised the pens. You'll still need me tomorrow, won't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Go home; I'm just finishing the rota.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can finish it. Put me wherever there's a gap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've given you Saturday off. You're part of the team, not emergency cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I'll train the emergency cover on Friday so you won't regret Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you put the pizza in, admire the oven. Four hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's spotless. Can I cook? I'm starving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Notice the rack as you slide it in. That was an hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy you dinner if we can keep it clean tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. We can toast the other three hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the empty detergent bottle beside your dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can it move? I need room for my plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. It represents six loads, if you're wondering.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six? I'll do the laundry tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Come and see how I fold the towels, so you know what you're taking on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tea, then shoes, then keys. You've picked up the keys before we've had tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're late for the train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we especially need the usual order. Otherwise we'll forget the tickets too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the tickets while you drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tickets go in after shoes. Please don't make us start packing again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Curtains, cat food, then our breakfast. Why's his bowl already down?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He woke me early. I fed him so you could sleep.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the curtains? Now he'll expect every meal before the day starts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll open them now. Your toast is ready too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it warm. We need him back at the bowl before we can safely have breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed two torches for our picnic, in case we get back after dark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm carrying lunch uphill. Use our phones and leave the torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. I'll bring power banks in case the phones die.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can carry those. My bag's full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One each, surely. If we get separated, you'd have all the sandwiches and no electricity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we drive to the campsite, where's the spare jack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought breakdown cover so we could stop packing tools.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll print their number in case your phone dies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a garage by the campsite. I'll walk there if necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then pack your walking boots. And leave me a map, in case I have to come and find you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shopping bag split. Lovely, now we can sort dinner before we get home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tomatoes are crushed. I wanted sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've accidentally started pasta sauce. You always say we should cook together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you let me handle the seasoning this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Try that chilli I always veto. I'll grate the cheese and learn to be surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plumber's cancelled. Lovely, we can finally have lunch together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sink still leaks. I've put a bucket under it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. The bucket's covering the sink; I'll set the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs emptying every ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll have courses. Neither of us can rush off with a sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Confetti sounds lovely for our wedding. Who's vacuuming it on Monday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll do it. Please let me have the confetti.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then yes. I'll put you down for Monday morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're flying to Venice at six. I'll ask my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask before we book. I need to know whether I'm packing sandals or the vacuum attachment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want three extra tables at the party. Who carries them home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can borrow a van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who returns the van?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I will. Can we put the deposit on your card?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I need the return time. Those tables are staying on my bill until the van gets home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we cut our wedding cake, that cherry's stem needs straightening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already called everyone over. Two hundred people are standing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they'll see the top clearly. Turn the stand towards me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our photographer leaves in two minutes. Please get beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask her for a close-up of the stem first. We can have our portrait taken on someone's phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over the house keys, can we straighten that hallway frame?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The buyers are waiting. Our taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're standing right under it. They'll think we left it like that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They just hung it. It's theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give them the keys. I'll stay and show them how to look after the frame.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wireless printer needs a cable to get started. They lure you in with 'wireless'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just for setup. Then enter the password underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So their next step is turning it upside down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll lift it. You read the label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now their simple setup needs staff. Hold it there; I'll fetch my glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This replacement bulb needs a different fitting. They've made changing a bulb a renovation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's an adapter. I'll order it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how they get you. The bulb is just the invitation to buy more parts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Delivery's free if we spend another ten pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now we have to expand the repair to afford finishing it. What else have they broken?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Green suits our hallway. That's settled; I'll get the rollers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I live here too. Can we try my blue sample?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your appeal can have one square beside the radiator.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. We'll ask our daughter which she prefers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She can hear the appeal. I'll explain why green won before you show her the square.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we order soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're choosing our own lunches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your appeal is denied. Separate bills don't overturn the soup ruling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already paid for a sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm amending the ruling to include a starter. Order the soup before they bring your sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All deliveries go round the back. You'll have to move that trolley.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did the building manager approve that? This fridge barely fits the front door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can make an exception for your fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll show her your badge and ask where she wants it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's keep her out of the lifting. You choose the entrance; I'll take the heavy end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm setting the rehearsal order. Solos first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did the director ask you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She values initiative. We could begin with your solo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need. An ensemble opening suddenly feels more inclusive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before joining our cheese panel, identify this rind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just came to eat cheese.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then identify it for the tasting queue. Judging requires the county certificate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have that certificate. I teach the county course.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Before you examine our cheese, let me examine your syllabus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may judge the garden competition once I check your pruning certificate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm filling in for my wife. She's broken her ankle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me where you'd cut this rose. We can assess you here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She could judge by video. I'll carry the phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. First demonstrate that you can distinguish a diseased leaf from a blurry one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is someone sitting in my chair at the founders' dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's a sponsor. Have you brought your founder's invitation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You need an envelope to establish that I founded this place?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know you did. I'll bring another chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For him, thank you. Put mine back at the head.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my nameplate on the allotment committee chair. Let's start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you got the result sheet? I need to verify who's chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want me to prove I'm entitled to my own chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call the secretary. She can confirm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put her on speaker. Once she's confirmed me, I'll ask her to minute your apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm opening an hour later. You won't have to come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check timetable changes with me first. Regulars need continuity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll explain it to them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good practice. I'll stand beside you and handle any questions about the hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, staff rotas won't need your approval anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already told the staff to send their rotas directly to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them I'll do the final review beside you. You should see how approval works before abolishing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love your exhibition to happen. I haven't signed the room form yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The installer needs it by four. Is there anything I can change?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing. It's lovely. I just need to feel ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll book the other gallery. They don't need your signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll gladly introduce you. Let me approve the email before you send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The youth club trip sounds wonderful. I've helped finish the coach booking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks. We just need your funding code.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll send it when I'm comfortable releasing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit with you while you check the figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How kind. The figures are fine. You can help me write a reassuring update while everyone waits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We started on the same biscuit-packing line. Pass the biscuits, Director.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please use my title at work. The new staff are here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. This is the director. We shared my lunch when he forgot his.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you tell them something more recent?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's sharing today. Pass that tin, mate; I'll do the introductions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pulled my chair beside yours for the induction. Like our first day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing myself as their manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce us together. We spent our first morning looking for the toilets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You show them around after my welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come with me. You found the toilets; I found the kitchen. We still make one useful employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought your bakery mixer. Save me a place at the menu tasting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a birthday gift, not a share in the bakery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I backed your cakes. I should taste what my support produces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're switching to bread. Come Friday; the customers will choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll come Thursday. They should only choose between loaves I've approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before changing the club name, remember who paid the deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've paid you back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The money, yes. I still backed the club we're naming.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The printer needs a name today. Pick between these two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me see the rejected names too. My support deserves more than the final round.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As assistant director, I've costed both sets. The garden fits our budget.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So does my kitchen. Give the director both designs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll put the garden sketch on the cover to brighten the pack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use a plain cover. We can each present our design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll schedule you both. The garden designer can go first while you're setting up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The captain's finishing her briefing. As first mate, I'm collecting harbor updates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: North harbor's closed. South and west both have berths available.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flag the closure immediately and attach my recommendation for west.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll report the options myself. I haven't recommended either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll introduce you and bring both berth sheets. West's booking form is already filled in; I'll leave it beside her pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I fixed the office kettle. Put that in my column for next manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no vacancy. Sam bought the replacement fuse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give Sam procurement. Give me delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You two could fix the toaster together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll coordinate Sam. We can finally compare technical ability with leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam's missed the stock meeting. Another point to me for next manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's unloading the delivery. Cancel the meeting and help him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll record my attendance, then my flexibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam asked for you specifically. He says you're good at stacking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that under endorsements. I'll stack beside him so we can see whose pile stays up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check my wedding speech again. Just punctuation this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cut the divorce joke. The bride's parents separated last month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that's why I flagged it. What should replace it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use my story about them getting lost on their first date. Credit me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll thank you for proofreading. How does your story end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which road gets us to the wedding? I'm checking my choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: East. The west bridge is closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As I thought. Which east turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Give me the map and let me navigate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can hold it. I'll make the decisions. Is this the turn?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time someone moved lunch, they held the meeting without me. Why move it again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sandwich delivery's late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what they said while electing my replacement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then we'll eat in here. You can keep chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put the sandwiches beside me. Last time everyone followed whoever had the platter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You crossed out my tea order, Pat. Last year it was my shed proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only need twenty cups. You ordered forty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how the committee started calling my judgment unreliable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write that the attendance changed. This isn't a vote on you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Put that last sentence in the minutes too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pause silenced the committee. I'll copy it for my report. Annoying how easily that works for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was holding back a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your cough commands respect. How long did you hold it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just say, 'I'd like your attention.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your attention. Was that your exact tone? You make four words look hereditary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got us this table with one raised eyebrow. Show me. Must be nice having that face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I raised the left one. But please just ask for the bill; I'm late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left. Like this? You barely moved yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming. Keep it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got a table in a second. I'm getting a cramp asking for paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought my headteacher's bell to the retirement lunch. Shall I ring everyone into their seats?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. I promised the caterers we'd start at one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the register. I'll find who's holding us up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a buffet. Your former colleagues can serve themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll appoint table monitors. They can report to me before anyone takes seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings over. I've put out my counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold me the shop last year. I count them now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Bring your total and I'll check it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I came to invite you to our anniversary sale.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Already a year? Leave me the proposed discounts. I'll approve them before you print.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch as supervisor. If I order soup, will they think promoting me was a mistake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promoted you. I'm having soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then soup. Unless copying you proves I can't lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Choose mine too. I need to take this call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both lunches? Right. Does choosing the bread count toward whether I keep the job?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the delivery form. Was my signature managerial enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs to be legible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they've lowered the standard for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, it's the same form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll practise until I deserve the same form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrow my car. I'll feel better if we agree every stop first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just my sister's, then home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Text before leaving hers so I can approve the traffic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She might need me to stay overnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Give me her number; I'll arrange your bedtime so you're safe to drive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fund your exhibition. Let me choose the guests so nobody undermines you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need critics there. That's how I get another show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send me their names. I'll find the encouraging ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The main critic won't promise a good review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit beside her. You can concentrate on being independent while I handle her questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. That means I can sit at her table, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating donors. She says hello to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me again. If she remembers me, you'll know I belong there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked you to bring over that empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She picked me. I'll carry it over and ask which side of her I should sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm photographing her team. She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her my name. She should know who she's trusting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now she wants you to bring her bag to the car. You're blocking my shot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take both. Ask if she wants me beside her in the car. She clearly needs me on the team.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note about my rescue of the accounts was lovely. Will you read it at the staff lunch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote it privately because you hate speeches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Giving them. Hearing one about my work is quite different.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no microphone. I can thank you at our table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Let's move our table into the middle so nobody misses your thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you introduce me as Chair at the committee picnic?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thanked you for chairing when you arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very warmly. Unfortunately, everyone else was unpacking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask you to pass the sandwiches. They'll hear your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say, 'Our Chair will now serve lunch.' Then I'll wait for them to look up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing beside the teaspoons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical proximity is not authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I lend you this ladder, your department head must ask mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're neighbours, cleaning gutters. My wife sent me over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then her request should go to my wife. I can supply the ladder's dimensions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your wife's away. She left you in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then address it to me as acting head. I'll forward it to her for confirmation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together. I just want everyone fed before the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together isn't a name. The children are opening crisps—who can tell them to wait?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, you're in charge of lunch. Sam's running the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop his whistle. Who's in charge if a game runs into lunch? We need one name now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager's gone. Wait—who's in charge of the kettle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Anyone. I'll make tea while you lock up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're in charge. I'll tell everyone before I touch the doors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only until my taxi comes. It's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Name your replacement before you get in. We can't have boiling water between administrations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put me on the broken printer? I'll need purchasing authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs paper. There's a box by my desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move it to mine and manage supplies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Then everyone will come to you when they run out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Have them bring their print jobs too, so I can decide which ones get priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tenants rejected my bike shed proposal? I'll chair the review.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No review. Just send everyone the result; I need to book next month's meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect replies too. You need someone who knows what residents want.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, but you'll have to read forty emails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll draft your agenda. I'll know which complaints deserve the meeting's time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely ribbon-cutting. Our freezer delivery is outside; who can unlock the building?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chief executive wants us both in the photograph first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can she let the freezers in? Photograph us while she unlocks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only the caretaker has keys. He's leaving in her car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep her posing, then. I'll get the caretaker to open up before she needs her car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your title's impressive. Can you release the repair funds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My deputy handles finance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I speak to the powerful part of this office?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I make the big decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Decide to introduce me to the cheque book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm wearing the barbecue apron. I decide when the burgers turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my apron.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should respect its office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That would be a transfer of power. Finish your petition first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have the meeting bell. That means I'm chairing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bicycle bell.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet you stopped talking when I rang it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I finish deciding whether you may.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fetched her coffee. So she's above you on the chart.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was being nice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unpaid tribute. A very secure position for her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She fetched mine yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is a rotating monarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone looked at the quiet man before approving the budget. He must run this place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's the electrician. The lights flickered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the director waited for his nod. So he's above her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's stopping the meeting to let him out. Can we please finish?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once she returns. Apparently even his departure outranks our budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asking for your spare key back tells me we're frightened of getting closer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm frightened of paying for a third lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I understand us better than that. I'll keep the key; we need to practise trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then trust me with your spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Exchanging keys is exactly the commitment I knew we were ready for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our dinner silence means we're comfortable together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm angry about your joke. Cancel tomorrow's dinner with your sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Telling me proves we're secure. Dinner stays; we're ready for family.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you're explaining to her why I'm silent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll explain that you trust her with your anger. I'll ask her to seat you beside her; we're ready for that closeness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made soup. We can have a perfectly calm dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss why I slept in the spare room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After soup. I'll handle dinner; we don't need to disturb anything tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hand is shaking. Let me carry that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You pour. I'll hold the tray with both hands. We can still carry dinner in together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your mother's letter under the fruit bowl. We'll discuss her moving in after a peaceful lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's bringing her suitcase at two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll serve another course. We have everything under control.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can call and ask her to wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Say we're enjoying lunch. Nothing about us needing more time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tapped your cup three times. You're about to ask for money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm waiting for the tea to cool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the story you used before the bicycle loan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Actually, I brought the bicycle money back. I've counted it twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twice means you want me to refuse it, like your rent money. Keep it; I'll make your usual celebratory tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You chose the chipped mug. Bad news, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my favourite mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You held it through the whole story about losing our deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll use a glass. Can we just have tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only change cups when I've guessed. I'll sit down for this one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've hung my coat on my old hook. What's for dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved out three years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hook didn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We use that space for guests now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the guests their hook has an owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my usual chair at the club table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your membership expired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You saved this seat for me every Thursday for twelve years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can sign you in as my guest tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Put yourself down as mine next week; we always take turns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our Tuesday agreement says whoever cooks doesn't wash up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know you kept it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We both signed beside the spaghetti stain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we change it? You used every pan tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what I said after your lasagne. We agreed the cook soaks the pans. Shall I start there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take the car, our note says we call each other first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were asleep. Mum needed collecting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We allowed that when your dad missed the last bus. Same exception?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, but please stop saving these on takeaway menus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fair. Let's copy the exception into our phones before the curry price changes again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your guests arrive, could we settle which version of last summer I'm remembering?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The one where you watered my plants.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll leave your envelope in my drawer, then. Could we talk upstairs?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm supposed to be welcoming people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll welcome them while you find us a quiet room. Plants are such a safe subject.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your toast at my wedding dinner, I've still got the key to our old keepsake box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't tell my parents about the resignation letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'd appreciate the same care with the story about my first marriage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the opening. What am I supposed to say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with how well we keep each other's confidence. Your parents will like that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Purple umbrellas. Please tell me our old escape signal still works at your office parties.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're divorced. And that meant order dessert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember the menu version. With the eyebrow, it means rescue me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get you a taxi after pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pudding, then rescue. You still speak it better than I do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps: rescue me from this reunion speech. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the headteacher now. I wrote it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm still the person you signalled when assembly ran long.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cut a paragraph. Keep your glass still; you're distracting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One glass down, one paragraph gone. We still get each other out of assembly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed all night when your business failed. Are you borrowing against the house again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a small loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At four in the morning, 'small' meant your entire savings. I deserve the figure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll show you the application. You don't get a veto.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me before you sign. That night earned me a conversation while there's still a choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drove through that storm for you. Don't give me the polite refusal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm genuinely busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what with. I earned a noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The road's repaired. My expectation of honesty hasn't.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're crying, love. I'll make tea and ring your manager, like last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, I've been promoted. Could you just listen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Will they give you enough staff?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Just raise your cup and say congratulations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations. Now, who covers you when you're ill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're late for Mum's birthday again. I've told her your train broke down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling her I overslept. You always cover for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll explain how exhausted you've been.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just come in with me. Don't explain anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll look exhausted too. She'll see it runs in the family.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam's photo has a bigger frame than mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a bigger photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you had room for more Sam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can buy matching frames.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if mine doesn't look like compensation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clare's wedding invitation has a ribbon. Mine has a staple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I gave you the first one, before the ribbon arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So Clare got the version you were proud of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take my ribbon. I'm the bride.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will Clare know? Otherwise she'll still think you like her more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which key opens my new flat? Sorry, you haven't been there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You chose it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Which pocket would I have put the key in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left, usually. Put a hook by the door so you won't need to ring me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. How high should the hook go? You've never seen the door. I'll send you a photo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which coat for my interview? Sorry, I still ring you before opening the wardrobe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Blue. It's still here, but I'm leaving for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you bring it? I've made you my wardrobe department again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave it at reception. You'll have to introduce yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What should I say? No, don't come in. Just stay on the phone until they've met me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm nearly over you missing my birthday. Shall we book dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thursday, unless work needs me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said before I ate both birthday puddings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friday, then. I'll put a reminder in my phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Make it say my name. Last year's just said 'dinner'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your flowers here. I'm nearly over the vase, honestly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In a mug? Harder for me to improve the decor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said that while I picked up Mum's signature. Still, flowers are a lovely start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry. I forgot she'd painted it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Never mind. Let's find water. You did choose the blue with her, though. I kept that piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You arrive at family lunch empty-handed and everyone hugs you. It's lovely. I've baked three cakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'd hug you without cake. Come sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you introduce me before mentioning the cakes? Give me a fair start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my brother. They know you. Leave the cakes here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All three? Fine. Save me whichever seat gets hugged first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our new housemates adore your sleepy hello. It's wonderful. Unfair, but wonderful. Listen to mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm making breakfast. Just say hello.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hello. Lovely people. Would you choose to live with that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We already chose you. Pass the toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Did you hear how naturally I said that? You could wake up to it daily.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on our old driving song. Shall we take the coast road?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used to get lost there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I was adventurous then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You complained for forty miles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With chemistry. Let me try the opening complaint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wore the scarf from our first photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't fit your coat anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It fits the person you met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to be that person.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just until dessert. He knew how to make you laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You took longer to answer my message today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was in a meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A meeting I used to hear about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me one boring detail so I know there's still room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said maybe to Friday dinner. Should I stop keeping your chair clear?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to check my shift. I've asked for Friday off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Off work, or off coming here every week?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Off work. Can we eat at seven? I need an early night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Seven's fine. Shall I serve pudding with the main so you don't have to stay for another course?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Text when you and Ben reach the cinema, love, so I know you're safe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my phone stays off during the film.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When does it finish? I'll wait up for your message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're walking to dinner afterwards. We haven't chosen anywhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive behind you while you choose. You can keep your phone off; I'll see for myself that you're having a nice time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your train snacks. Send me a photo of the departure board so I know you're all right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone's nearly dead. I've written down the platform.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which platform? I'll watch the departures here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Platform six. Can you bring a charger instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll stay until you're charged enough to send updates all the way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Should I use my chipped mug or one of the guest cups?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I used to know without asking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chipped one's still yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll leave it beside yours, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've still got you as my emergency contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine like paperwork, or fine like you'd come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd come.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll stop hovering over the delete button.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're putting my little boat in the wedding slideshow? Remember making it by the lake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm cutting that slide. Nobody will know what it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could mention who stood in the rain finding its mast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only got room for a short caption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'Alex stayed until I stopped crying.' They don't need the boat-building details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's my sleeve in your graduation photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You caught me when I tripped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Funny how the sleeve made the official album.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember the person in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me that bit. The sleeve's heard enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we sign the shop over, two spoons. We always share dessert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ordered my own. We're allowed separate puddings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. One shared bite first. We're selling the shop, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's coming in a takeaway box. My train leaves soon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll walk you to the station. Keep both spoons out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave for university, we haven't finished our handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the last move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knuckles, then thumbs. You can move out without us becoming people who just wave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The driver's charging by the minute now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it on my card. I'm paying for the knuckle tap, not a longer goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancelled lunch. Should I leave my key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have a dentist appointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch, then the key, then separate dentists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For emergencies or belonging? I'm choosing which ring it goes on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my chair away from yours. Shall I pack the books too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was vacuuming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Clearing my corner first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it back. You can choose where.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside yours. Unless letting me choose means you're keeping your options open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You gave me my chipped plate. We're still us, even with your bags packed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only clean plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you gave it to me. Still looking after me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Eat before it gets cold. The gravy's separate, like you prefer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the gravy too. I'll set your place. We can discuss the bags over dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're dividing our records and you still laughed at my terrible joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a funny joke. It doesn't settle who gets the jazz.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can disagree over jazz and still get each other. Dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One drink. Your usual?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember that too. Make it a double; I think we can manage the jazz together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can be angry and still choose a Tuesday to talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A diary won't fix this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It gives the fixing somewhere to happen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what I'll say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll start at six with not knowing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know visiting after our row feels awkward. Would a spare key help?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not the door. I need to know you actually want me here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fair. I'll invite you for Sunday lunch. The key can wait.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lunch, yes. But I need to leave by two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two it is. I'll serve pudding at one. No negotiating with you in your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note says I'm 'welcome for now.' Should I unpack?

beats.speaker: B
