beats.text: Yes. I meant until your flat's repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'for now' instead of 'until the repairs'? Is your welcome wearing out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross it out. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But 'for now' was there before I complained. What happens when I stop asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said we're 'still friends' while taking me off the pub quiz team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friends. We just need someone who knows sport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You dropped 'still.' Does that mean friendship's the consolation prize for losing my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come Thursday anyway. I'll save you a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the team we're 'still friends.' I want to hear which word you stress in public.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Third time this week outside the bakery. Fate clearly wants us to catch up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live on the same street.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. It keeps putting us within talking distance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm moving tomorrow. This is my last loaf here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it caught us just in time. Give me your new address before it has to start again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We both reached for this coat. First reunion in ten years, and the universe won't let us leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's mine. Yours is still on the rack.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it borrowed your coat to stop me missing you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's yours. Come on, we can share the taxi queue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coats, now taxis. It's arranging this in stages. Where are you headed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we lower the birthday banner? I'm having a complicated morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I'd like to approach it at a manageable height.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we at least sing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Begin softly. I'll let you know when we reach happy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your good news, I need everyone to understand my afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I got the promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Hold that feeling while I finish the parking story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're waiting on a video call for us to toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me on first. They need the parking story, or my face will look like a comment on your promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the delivery meeting. We're in control. Keep your voice just there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's missing. I'm trying not to panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep trying. We'll establish its last location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fetch the driver. He's shouting in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brief him outside first. Then sit beside me and give the report in your voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding's under control. Tell me about the cake in that lovely calm voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's leaning. I can hold the stand level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A minor adjustment. Keep talking like that while you hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll have to help. My hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll steady it together. You count us in; your voice hasn't started shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said dinner was fine while folding your napkin. That's guarded resentment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means the napkin was untidy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're restoring order because you feel unheard. Tell me what you needed from dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To eat without being analysed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good boundary. Now say it without hiding behind the napkin, so I can acknowledge it properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're laughing very quickly at Dad's impression. Nervous about meeting my parents?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, the impression was funny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's approval-seeking. You can let a joke pass without earning your place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you pass the biscuits? I missed lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Comfort-seeking now. Say 'I belong here' before you take one. Let's feed the insecurity first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I worked through three winters to open this shop. Leave me a chair at the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only investors are invited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cracked hands invested before the cheque books arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The form only accepts money. Could you speak under an investor's name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three winters in an unheated shop, and I need a sponsor? Put frostbite under capital. I'm speaking under my own name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I slept outside this theatre for two nights. Please let me finish my audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A verse is enough. We need the room for the next applicant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two nights on those steps earned me one chorus indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can finish in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring the panel. I didn't sleep outside to have my big moment overheard through a door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first restaurant review? When mine came, I made tea before opening it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've opened it. Two stars. I'm ringing the critic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the stage where I unplugged my phone. Milk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already dialled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let it ring while the tea brews. You're rushing a mistake I took all afternoon over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went through redundancy before you. First, tidy your desk slowly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm actually excited to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Early stage. I recognise the optimism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another job. They want me there Monday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday? I started too soon after mine. Leave a mug here; you're not ready to make a clean break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You forgot the concert. That's all right. I kept your ticket until the interval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take you next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's kind. I'll buy mine, and you can decide nearer the time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy both. Put it in my calendar now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both tickets. How lovely. I'll put my name in the reminder too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely to hear from you, love. I took the phone to bed at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my shift ran late. I'll call at eight tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eight would be lovely. I won't keep the evening clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can promise ten minutes on my break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten minutes. That's thoughtful. I'll save the important things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This napkin still says we'll open a bookshop by the sea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We drew that before rent became real.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We also drew two chairs by the window. Could we put ours together tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In the flat? I need to work at that window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After work, then. I'll bring our books. Ten minutes pretending we're in our seaside bookshop before we look at the bills.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when this jar was for our anniversary at the seaside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We spent the money on the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We promised we'd swim together. The boiler didn't cancel that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's in three weeks. We can afford the bus to the reservoir.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the bus fare in the jar. I'll pack the towels; we're still coming home with wet hair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You lent me this scarf when my marriage ended. Tell me honestly: should I answer his message?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't decide that for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You didn't decide anything that night. You stayed. Tell me what worries you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That you'll spend tonight waiting for another message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while I leave it unanswered. I'll make us tea this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sat with me when my shop closed. Will you help at the new stall? An honest answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know. My own shop's struggling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then forget the stall. You let me talk for hours when mine went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we sit without talking first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. You gave me three silent evenings. I've kept this one free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made everyone tea. I'll call Dad's friends about the funeral.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's good the calls don't require trays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit down. I'll call. Just give me their numbers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll dial for you. Peter will cry; I'll stay on the other phone in case you need rescuing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the last tissue. Mum's funeral was hard on you. I've got my sleeve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're crying into both sleeves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're washable. How's your daughter holding up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asleep. Come here. You can cry on my shoulder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll need that shoulder when she wakes. I'll get you a dry cardigan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One publisher turned you down? I've kept fourteen rejection letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you put them away? I came here for a hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Though fourteen rejections ought to qualify me for more than one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come here. We can both have the same hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make it a long one. One rejection's worth for you, and thirteen more before you let go of me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've been unemployed a week. I've been out a year. This coffee should really be for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought it so you'd listen to what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll listen. Mine will take longer; there's twelve months to cover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ten minutes each. I've got an interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An interview already? Then give me fifteen. You've started recovering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay seated while I open this letter. Your face looks reassuring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can open it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Keep looking like that while I prove it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what's inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You weren't supposed to let your face hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me while I open the audition result. You've stopped smiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm squinting at the screen. You haven't opened it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. So nothing's wrong. Move closer; the text is small.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm smiling now. Whatever it says, we'll get lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. I can click it now. This chair was the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we use any cups except the blue ones today?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened with a blue cup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing breakfast needs to revisit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Behind the plates, please. The handle's still looking this way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you move that yellow envelope away from my birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a voucher from your sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. My eviction notice came in yellow. I'll find her a nicer envelope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the voucher out and bin this one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Under the coffee grounds, please. I'll hold the lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You opened your rejection letter straight away. Must be nice, being brave on demand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was scared too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hid it very efficiently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take your time with yours. I'll leave you alone to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, stay. I'm opening it now. You shouldn't get to be brave and considerate while I'm still finding the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told them how you felt without rehearsing. I resent how impressive that was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stumbled over half of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your stumbling looked courageous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Want to practise with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Don't make practising look easy too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written when our shop opens. Before the first one failed, I never wrote if.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't afford another empty opening party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bake. I used to assume people would come for my cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six portions. That's our budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six generous portions. I'm writing 'come early' on the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm entering the talent show. At seventeen I invited everyone before I'd even chosen a song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you lost and wouldn't sing for a year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm borrowing the version before that. Will you come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Shall we sit at the back so you can slip out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Front row, please. Seventeen-year-old me expected to spot her friends from the stage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You moved our meeting to Friday. I've brought a box for my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a promotion. You'll manage the new branch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away from everyone? I'll pack before they have to say goodbye.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can still come to Friday drinks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring my own glass. Better get used to being a visitor before they stop inviting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You paused when I asked about Saturday. Should I collect my things from your flat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was swallowing tea. I'm taking you to dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Somewhere public. I'll bring tissues that fit in my sleeve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's at home. I'm cooking your favourite.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bring containers. You shouldn't have my leftovers haunting the fridge afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the letter from the college. You've already had one disappointment today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, it's my application.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And if it's another rejection, I'll tell you after you've eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see 'Congratulations' through the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then after your brother's eaten. He didn't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the condolence calls about Dad. You haven't slept.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to speak to Aunt June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll check whether she's crying before I put her through.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants me to comfort her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll comfort her first. You can have each other once I've got you both steady.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is my stool too close? I don't want you regretting our duet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're fine there. I need to see the music.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move behind you. You won't have to look at me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I can't see you come in. Sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside you. Good. Could you nod before each entrance so I know you still want me joining in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First dates don't need this many jokes. I'll stop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I liked the one about your dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just dog stories, then. I can do that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd like to hear about you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll start with who I was before the dog. Too far back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You came to my solo show. Please stop saying 'brave' in that sad voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three people walked out. I wanted to buy you a drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I finished anyway. You can buy a drink for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll invite the cast next door. They're celebrating a sellout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell them I finished with no audience at all. Let's see them do that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the entire move myself. Please stop making that poor-you face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You must be exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Impressively exhausted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I bring you tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. In the mug marked champion, not survivor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we close the old café, one minute's silence for the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only a kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It worked here longer than either of us. Stand properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I unplug it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the minute. Don't interrupt its final shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over Mum's house keys, we say goodbye to her garden: roses, tree, shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I tell the story about her locking us in the shed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the tree. She planted that first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The buyers are waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them to the roses. If they're waiting for the keys, they can wait in the right order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sighed over dessert. I'll turn the music off so you can tell me what's wrong.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate too much. That's all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clear it away. You don't need guilt sitting in front of you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. You're making me nervous.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nervous? I'm sitting. Shall I cancel our guests before this gets worse?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hesitated before putting your veil on. Shall I send everyone out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The comb's caught in my hair. Help me untangle it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll free it. You shouldn't feel trapped on your wedding day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just hurry. We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your voice changed. I'll tell Mum we need ten minutes with nobody expecting anything of you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery thanked me for my paintings. Help me choose glasses for opening night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the automatic reply. Don't spend our rent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're expecting enough interest to automate. We should buy in bulk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll lend you six glasses. That's all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first sponsor. I'll put your name on the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've sold our first book. I'll extend the shop's opening hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You bought it yourself. I'm refunding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent service already. That brings people back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy one for my sister. Then we're closing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first gift order. I'll stay overnight wrapping the rest; tomorrow we won't have time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Opening night without the lead you wanted hurts. Water, or some space in my dressing room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water won't make me happy for her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It just means you can be furious without a dry throat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming to ask if I'm okay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ask her to wait until after the show. You only owe her your cues tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can be furious about the cancelled train and still have toast before we drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't think about food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wrap it. You can decide when we're on the road.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't spend the drive telling me to calm down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Directions only. The toast won't require a better attitude either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That half-wave outside tells me we're neighbours now, not friends.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had shopping in both hands. Help me with this bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Groceries are still allowed across the boundary, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm making your birthday dinner. Come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. But that wave says this is the last year you wanted to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You texted 'thanks.' for covering your shift. Are we just colleagues now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was rushing. You're my best man. Help me choose ties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plain black. That full stop makes this a formal appointment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your speech is after dinner. Tell the story about our disastrous holiday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll list the dates and expenses. That full stop says we're past finding it funny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the first time we've laughed since the inheritance row. Write down today's date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tripped over Mum's footstool. I couldn't help it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I didn't mind. That's when we became sisters again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Can we finally sort her furniture?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start a new list. That footstool reunited us; it doesn't go on the inventory from when we hated each other.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, I said no to extra potatoes and didn't feel guilty. Put today's date on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left potatoes last Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was fullness. This is independence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Serve your own gravy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first unsupervised gravy. Pass me a clean plate; that one's from before.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The organiser left me the picnic briefing. You can tell the drivers the departure time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need the destination for their satnavs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send them to me individually. I'll disclose one postcode per driver.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're all sharing one minibus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nominate one driver. I'll tell him outside. The others can discuss the departure time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bride left me these envelopes. You can announce the tables, but not who's sitting together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating the guests. They need names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me one guest at a time. I'll release their chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I at least take couples together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me which couple. I'll disclose whether they're still being seated as one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got tomorrow's inspection covered. Leave the folder with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does page four say we need two sinks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It requires an appropriate number for the operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plumber's here. Shall I ask him to read it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have him quote for one and two. I'll confirm which interpretation we're implementing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know why the shop alarm sounded. We can open on time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was it the back door or the motion sensor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The system detected activity in the relevant area.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring up the log. You can show me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read me your interpretation first. I don't want my findings influencing yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve your expenses: the receipt says four, your note says four-oh-five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a biscuit on the way back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's a second transaction missing from your account.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for it myself. Here, have the other one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two biscuits. I'll need to revise the timeline before I sign.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over the shop keys, why did you cross out cupboard and write shelf?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cleaner moved them onto the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When? I need the last confirmed sighting before we sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nine. I saw them there. She doesn't start until ten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then who moved them before she arrived? Get her on the phone; we now need two accounts of one shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass me the unredacted reunion plan. I'm family, not the public.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That page lists everyone's surprise presents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Family should get more than the visitor edition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It includes your present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me who chose it. I should know who considers me family.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does my club briefing have blacked-out names?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only the organising committee sees those.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stacked every chair for that committee. Surely I've earned the names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can apply next month. I'll sponsor you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Could you put one name in my copy now, so I know you're sponsoring a member?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first shift on the club door. I'll teach you half the secret handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't I need the whole thing to admit people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can greet them. I'll handle admission until you've progressed to the wrist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The president wants me to train tomorrow's doorman.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Teach him the fingers. I'll teach you the wrist while he waits outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to the club. Tonight I'll teach you rule one: discretion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The secretary gave me the whole rulebook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Keep it closed while we establish discretion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to proofread it before printing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then read me each sentence. I'll tell you which ones you're ready to understand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can help find your parcel. The van number starts with four; let's check my route first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are six vans starting with four.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only two end in seven. Mine passes both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, your route. Which van do we stop at?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to guide you. Take my overdue collection first, then I'll point it out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can trace your missing projector approval. It came from upstairs; shall we review my repair budget together?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was it the director or her deputy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The signature starts with M. Let's put repairs on today's agenda.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're on. Purchasing still needs the surname.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Move repairs before refreshments and I'll give you the name for the purchase order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me at the reunion. We became friends hiding the headmaster's bicycle behind that purple gate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the headmaster now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're still the only headmaster who knows where we'd hide it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll save you a seat, but I have to give the welcome speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then begin with 'purple gate.' Everyone else will hear a welcome; I'll know you're still talking to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we pack Mum's biscuit tin, knock twice. That was our first secret.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She knew we emptied it. She told me years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still kept our signal. There's my brother.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You take the tin. We hardly see each other now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then knock twice when you visit. I'll know you're here for our tin, even if it's full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told Dad you were with me when you dented his car. Tell him I didn't break his greenhouse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was ten years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten years I've kept your evening accounted for. I need one afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't lie. I'll come with you while you tell him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit beside me. If he calls me careless, remind him how reliable I've been for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show me next month's private rota. I told the manager you were making deliveries when you missed that shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thanked you. I can't give you the manager's password.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You trusted me with a whole missing afternoon. I only want to see Saturdays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll check your Saturdays myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And put us together. If anyone questions it, say I'm someone you can rely on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you explain the broken window to Mum, give me your versions. Like last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said football. Jamie said the wind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we start with the broken window and our offer to pay. Leave weather out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jamie already texted her about a storm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the repair quote. I'll send something useful before she asks which storm plays football.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've peeled the surprise-party labels off the boxes by her desk. Same rescue service as last year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you. I told her they're printer supplies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll move the balloons before she asks which printer takes helium.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She offered to unpack them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her I'll handle it. She already thinks I do all the office jobs; we can keep the cake under that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've solved your missing parcel. Tracking says reception; you were still refreshing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for three boxes. Only two reached our office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one stayed downstairs. I've narrowed your whole building to one desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The trolley's here. There's a box wedged underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it left reception but never got unloaded. You've found the parcel; I've solved why we've been calling reception all morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our mystery judge is the baker. Flour on the invitation. Solved before you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The miller uses flour too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's the miller. I've already moved past the obvious answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the envelope flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker, licking it after decorating. I've got the identity and the sequence; you've got ingredients.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close the office door. I hated the director's presentation. You're the only person I can say that to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asked me to collect feedback.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as engaged. This is just us having coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave your comments out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. The standing ovation felt like a hostage video. More coffee?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're the only one who's read my notebook. I don't want to take over Dad's shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He wants me to bring it to Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the accounts notebook. This one's mostly spelling mistakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep this one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I add something? I was relieved when the freezer broke. Terrible spelling on that page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we book our anniversary trip, why did you leave Venice early?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stay the whole week this time. Nonrefundable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You paid for the last night then, too. What happened?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum was ill. She asked me not to tell anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could have said that afterwards. When you said you needed space from me, was that her request too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll renew my club membership once you explain why my curtain vote vanished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're voting on curtains again. You can choose first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where will you put my choice this time? Last year's blue never reached the minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make you minute secretary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my first entry is 'Previous vote still unaccounted for.' Who can answer that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told the manager you hadn't lost the keys and he believed you instantly. How do you do that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hadn't lost them. I need you to tell him that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With my face? You get innocence; I get follow-up questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stand beside you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Could you look impressed when I tell the truth? Yours carries more weight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your hands stayed still when the treasurer asked about the missing cash. Mine made me look guilty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put them in your pockets. We both need to finish these statements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You get believed naturally. I need special trousers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here, hold my statement. That'll keep them busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your paper looks innocent. Can mine go underneath it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take Dad's fake trophy out of the cabinet, can I look at our photo?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look so proud of him in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was a lovely person to be. I thought he'd beaten twelve cyclists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can keep the photo without displaying the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we put it by my bike? I started riding that afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could the club's victory bunting stay up until tea? I liked us before we knew about the altered scores.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The visiting team arrives in ten minutes. We owe them the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I just remember hanging this with you. We hugged on a stepladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold it while you take the bunting down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hug me first? Same ladder. Less to celebrate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why did everyone stop talking when I came into the staff kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'd finished choosing lunch. Do you want noodles?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is noodles what you're calling the thing I'm not supposed to know?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Look, here's the order. Yours is already on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You decided what I'd want before I arrived. How long have you been discussing me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both notebooks closed when I sat down for the rota meeting. Am I being replaced?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine has my medical appointments in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And does Jen keep your appointments too, or did you agree on that explanation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask Jen about hers. You aren't reading mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So she's handling questions and you're guarding the records. When was that decided?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the landlord's letter once you're sitting down. You've only just got home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's addressed to me. Is he selling our flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's get you out of this doorway before we discuss where we'll live.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sitting. Give it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your favourite chair. Come to the kitchen; I'd rather you didn't remember this whenever you sit there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the last page of the review after your concert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does it say anything about my voice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It says things you don't need to carry onto a stage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then give it to me in the interval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's before your solo. I'll bring you water in the interval. Water hasn't formed an opinion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told me about the move before your family. I thought that meant we were especially close.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We are. I'm telling them tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you call me just before? One last conversation where it's ours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come to dinner. You can help me tell them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you say I already knew? I want to sit beside you, not among the surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is there another chair? I thought only I knew you were selling the bakery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's buying it. He needs to see the accounts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. You told me because we're close; he's getting spreadsheets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll need to know why I'm selling, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell me how you feel about telling him before he arrives? That part could still be ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you brief the volunteers, every escaped rabbit used the east gate. I spotted that Tuesday, if a timeline helps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were right. I'll tell them to check that latch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mention Tuesday so they understand how long this was preventable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come explain the check yourself. I need to catch the rabbits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Could you introduce me as the person who spotted it? Saves explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my Tuesday note beside the leaking freezer. It identifies the overnight power cuts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. The engineer needs the times, not our names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My initials distinguish observed times from later guesses. Purely useful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then write the repair request yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. 'Following my Tuesday discovery' gets the chronology settled before we trouble him with temperatures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write the password before I hand over the surprise picnic sandwiches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're alone in the kitchen, and the bus leaves in two minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write quickly. Speaking it cancels collection.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've written cucumber. That's yesterday's password, isn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've said it. The sandwiches stay here. I'll tell the walkers their lunch failed clearance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signal Mum's birthday cake location: three fingers for cupboard, four for fridge. Say it aloud and you're off the surprise team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the table. The helpers need to find it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're off. Table is a flat palm. I'll signal them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already sent them a photo. That doesn't say anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It shows everything. Now we move the cake and change the signals. You won't be told where your slice is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The florist asked what time our surprise party starts. How did it get out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told her so she'd deliver before Dad arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now the driver knows. Can you collect the flowers yourself?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I'll ask the baker to give me a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's reached the baker while we were containing the florist. How many stops is this lift making?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why are there three copies of our private resignation letter on your desk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One for each of us and a spare. Nobody else has seen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The spare is a conversation waiting to happen. Shred it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I use the accounts shredder? Ours is jammed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts already? We haven't destroyed one copy and it's reached another department. Who there knows?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The budget page is missing from our club minutes. Someone's made accounts night interesting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer took it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. A suspect with homework. Shall we ring her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's here. She says she never took it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A contradiction in person! Bring her a chair beside mine; I'm staying for the whole meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You ordered our anniversary cake, but the baker says we cancelled. What an intriguing start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have the receipt. It says collected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancelled and collected! Let's ask who collected it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says you did. He has your signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I'm involved! Bring the receipt; this is much more personal than dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Dad's surprise picnic, where can forty guests board the bus unseen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Outside my shop. Dad never goes there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell everyone to arrive separately so the neighbours don't mention a crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's offered to open the shop for me while I organise it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then board at the library. Ring all forty guests; no group message Dad might see. Who's collecting him after we leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Mum's surprise party, we're saying you brought the cake on the nine o'clock bus?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. She'll ask why she didn't see my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The last bus leaves at eight. Can you claim you walked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She drove past me at half eight. I was empty-handed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the cake was already here. We need Dad to remember accepting it before his nap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The painting's gone. That red thread on its frame will explain everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My scarf caught there last night. Can we open the gallery?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This thread will date the theft. Was the painting there then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. But I picked that thread off before leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this one means someone came back wearing your scarf. Keep it on; we'll reconstruct the whole night from this snag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This coffee ring is the key to the missing keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The keys are in your pocket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain why the cup was beside them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now we have the movement sequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wardrobe isn't escaping. It's exercising its freedom of position.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's taking my work clothes down the road. Help me stop it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll escort it. Ask politely for your uniform; this is a free wardrobe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It wants rent for storing my shirts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a proposal, not a demand. Bring our tenancy agreement; a free wardrobe can negotiate its share of the bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our doorway opens to yesterday. It's an extension, not a fault.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yesterday's me is coming through to complain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first visitor. Please make our extension welcoming.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says this is his house and we're the visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's confusing age with ownership. Show him today's mortgage payment; visiting hours end at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the telescope ready. The moon will turn green at noon, exactly as I foretold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's noon. Still white.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Noon where the prophecy was written. We have six hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wrote it here. I lent you the pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An imported pen. The change will occur at its factory's noon. Keep watching while I check the label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Set our best plates out. A visitor wearing gold will bring us a fortune tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the plumber with brass fittings. I'll get his payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Working gold. Leave the money; he'll be bringing ours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His bill's enormous. We owe him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fortune changing hands. Fetch the chequebook; once he leaves, we'll never have to pay a plumber again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your ghost has reverse haunting: fear of occupied houses. We'll relocate it under a reassuring sheet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a sheet with little houses printed on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use a plain one. We mustn't transport the trigger with the patient.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plain one's fitted. It keeps pulling the ghost into a ball.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's involuntary apparition compression. Release the corners separately; we need it ghost-shaped for the doorway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the invisible creature's collar, measure below its second neck. The first one's decorative.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tape stops in midair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the chin shelf. Lower it two inches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's measuring me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reciprocal fitting. Stand straight and let it finish; interrupting produces a collar that fits both of you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've saved our invisible guest their usual chair. I remember everything from my trial dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the guest you're putting your coat on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The welcome draping, of course. I wanted my membership dinner to start properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're offering you their coat now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Mutual recognition. Help me find the sleeves; I'd hate to rush such an honour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can introduce me to your cloud family. I know the salute: this hand means welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's rain. Shall I tell them you're new?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need. The previous clouds used it differently. Your family will appreciate the traditional greeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mother's raining directly on you. Come under my umbrella.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And refuse her welcome? Hold my phone; I'll greet your father with both hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your first shadow banquet, bow until the host's shadow bows back. Take your time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You only nodded. Mine's still waiting, and dinner's starting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have a standing courtesy. Lower your head a little; let it see you mean it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's lying flat across the dining-room door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, a full welcome. Stay bowed while we step over; I'll bring your plate so you needn't offend it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To enter the mirror, introduce yourself backwards. Slowly; give your reflection time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You walked straight through. Could your reflection introduce me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We have a private arrangement. Try your surname first; I'll wait here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's asking yours how to get an arrangement. Neither will let me through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful conversation. Gently turn yours towards you; I'll distract mine. We'll practise introductions without discussing my terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm just serving soup. This spoon's the last utensil that hasn't melted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're starving, and the soup's floating out of reach. Let me use it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll catch it for everyone. Send the smallest children first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's rising towards the ceiling. I'll lift you if you feed my daughter next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm only the server; you're the legs. Carry me from child to child, and I'll portion what we catch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This kitchen tile still has gravity. I'm just keeping a place for everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pull me down. I can't hold the ceiling much longer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my hand. One foot on my tile, please; leave room for your dad.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's floating out the window. Let me take your place and reach him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay as the anchor. Nothing grand; climb onto my shoulders and I'll allocate the next foothold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Walk backwards to dessert, like every family Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've never done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say that before the backward part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spill my tea. Can you carry it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's why we link elbows. Gran always said nobody should reach pudding alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set the invisible ancestor's chair by the window again. Pass his plate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last chair. Where does my boyfriend sit?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On the piano stool, like every newcomer. Your father managed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought the pudding. Can't the ancestor share?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Pudding bearers sit on his lap. Put a cushion down, as usual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy your lunch today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Use that time to retrieve yesterday's minutes. Then we're square.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I helped move your sofa. Move the moon away from my window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those aren't equivalent favours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa had stairs. The moon's already airborne.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll move your bed away from the window. I have twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move the moon for twenty minutes each night. I didn't leave your sofa halfway upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your floating relatives still need place cards. I'll get string.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're floating through the ceiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need the upstairs seating plan too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. Aunt June can finally avoid Uncle Peter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if they stop on different floors. Which one ordered the vegetarian meal?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The fountain's producing wishes. Who empties the bucket?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a miracle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Miracles still overflow onto borrowed carpets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can wish the water away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put someone on hourly wishing duty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only bow to our invisible queen? I'm giving her my chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She already has an invisible throne.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine can support her feet. You hadn't considered her comfort.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give her my cushion, then. You can sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your cushion. She can have my bed. I'll sleep standing in case she calls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You signed the pledge that the moon hears us? I'll sign with both hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One signature's enough. I'm taking it outside tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll use two pens. She should know which of us means it twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's illegible. She won't know your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write it across my bedsheet. You can carry your little page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your backward walk boiled the kettle. Coincidence. How do I open this cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Compliment it. We need the cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely hinges. Very distinguished grain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. It's open. Now the fridge wants an apology before it'll release the milk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another coincidence. What exactly did I do to the fridge? I want to get this right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your formula says sing to the jammed printer. Payroll needs these now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It likes lullabies. Start softly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sleep, little printer, the stapler is near.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's printing. Keep going until the last payslip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coincidence. Sleep, little printer—write this tune on the troubleshooting sheet before you leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You promised me a sunrise in a box last anniversary. The shelf's still ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was poetic. I can bring you breakfast in bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Put the box beside the tray when it's ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It won't be ready this anniversary either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll leave the shelf clear another year. Please don't buy anything that needs that space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set a plate for that guest from next century you promised last Christmas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They can't arrive for another hundred years. We should eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go ahead. I'll keep their dinner warm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The oven won't last a hundred years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the replacement needs a warming drawer. Your guest is still expected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked that talking doorway for directions without hesitating. That's impressive. I usually just chat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then ask it where the toilets are. We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Morning, door. Usual question: toilets?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Through its ear. Give me a minute; I've never gone in that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left ear or right, door? You take your minute. I'll save you a cubicle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You greet invisible guests so easily. I wish I had your touch. Actually, I usually hug them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the umbrella stand. Martin's behind you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Martin! No formalities between us. Come for supper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I usually ask whether he can eat visible food first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, we can skip all that. Martin, help yourself from the fridge whenever. I'll get you a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring my old repair manual. Before all this, every kettle fault had a sensible cause.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's floating above your head. I need my tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loose bracket. My customers always called before things fell.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's pouring sideways into my cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pressure fault, then. Manual says disconnect it before servicing. Where's the plug?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I was caretaker, this door opened into the staffroom. What's all this Thursday business?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It opens into next Thursday. My coat's still in there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Calendar's been fitted backwards. I'll turn it round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's last Thursday. My coat hasn't arrived yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wrong-size calendar. Fetch the old one. We never lost a coat to a properly fitted door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call Mum's floating chair impossible. Reality might hear. Pass her the potatoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's above the table. I can't reach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just a high chair. Fetch the stepladder; dinner's getting cold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's at the ceiling now. I'm calling for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call it room service. Ask for a taller ladder and three desserts upstairs. We're having a perfectly ordinary family dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lower your voice about the singing moon. We don't want it noticing us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everybody can hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then call it weather. Weather gets away with anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's singing my name. Should I answer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only with 'Lovely evening.' Keep walking. We're just two people discussing the forecast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear this ribbon before dinner. It prevents emotional lightning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no such thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Doubt attracts it. You'll need a second ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hands are covered. I can't hold a fork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Metal conducts resentment. I'll feed you with a wooden spoon, after we insulate your opinions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Helmet on before reading the prophecy. We haven't inspected tomorrow for falling objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's one sentence. I just want to know if the picnic's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short prophecies concentrate the future. Read it through this oven glove.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It predicts sunshine. Surely that's safe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unfiltered future sunlight. Close the glove. Nobody reads another word until I've put sunscreen on tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on the new dragon! I was just about to clap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were gasping. It ate the shed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes! A devastating shed. I mean devastating loss.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you still clapping?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Checking whether we've moved into brave celebration yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely hilarious news about the mirror. Ha! Ha!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We weren't laughing. It's trapped the headmaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's my shocked laugh.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're trying to help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes! Help! I'm extremely ahead on wanting that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I predicted the cupboard would speak. Here: a change in storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That could mean new shelves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful prediction covers several forms of expression.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ink's wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fresh copy. Ancient certainty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My notes say something would rise. The floating dog confirms it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says bread will rise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An early metaphor for domestic elevation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wrote it while baking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspiration doesn't restrict itself to office hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you blow out your birthday candle, we need a witness candle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can that be the last one? The ice cream's melting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, once we acknowledge its service.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say thank you. Then we eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Light the acknowledgement candle so everyone can see you thanking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shoelace is tied. Now we bless the successful tying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bus is here. I'm finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The knot is finished. The departure requires a second knot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, I've double-knotted it. Can I go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After we formally introduce the two knots. They'll be travelling together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your lift notice says 'third loor.' A letter's gone; the building's unravelling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my typo. I need the lift for deliveries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me restore the F before you put any weight on that floor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's my marker. Oh, it's dried out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now matter's disappearing. Give me your delivery labels; I'll spell out every floor before we lose the stairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've said 'the rent's due' twice. Time's slipping in this flat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you didn't hear me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sound's failing too. We should tell the landlord.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I am the landlord. Shall I write it down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please. Date it, so we'll know whether tomorrow still arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kettle's floating! Tea no longer needs a table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone upstairs. I promised Mum breakfast in bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Direct delivery! We can retire the breakfast tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on her ceiling. She wants me to bring the tray back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, breakfast has an upstairs! I'll rig the tray on pulleys. Ask Mum how high she likes her toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our guest floated through the wall! Wonderful, the door queue is obsolete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She left a hole in the plaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A second entrance! Invite the neighbours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain's coming through. We'll need umbrellas at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Indoor umbrella seating! Finally, a seating plan with altitude. I'll move the chandelier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, a dragon in the kitchen. Dry food or wet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Treasure. I want to keep him, but my pocket money won't cover it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll buy in bulk. You handle feeding and cleanup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He breathes fire when he's hungry. Can you do mornings? I'm at school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take breakfast. We'll tile the feeding corner and put treasure deliveries before the school run.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The invisible guest can stay. Who takes the first feeding shift?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's immortal. I'm only house-sitting until Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me your routine before you leave. I'll arrange permanent weekend cover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't know if it eats. I've just been leaving sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Label Sunday's sandwich. I'll check weekly, and put the sandwich checks in my will.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our ferry's floating above the harbour. Keep that souvenir pebble level; it's the only thing stopping us tipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I picked it up for you. I need my hands for the bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my lunchbox. I'll keep the ferry level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your sandwiches make it tilt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flatten them into a level bed. Lunch can suffer; the passengers mustn't slide off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't press the kettle's third button. That tiny scratch on it is keeping the moon lit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the boil button. I want tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use a saucepan. We can't risk smoothing the scratch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll press it with my fingernail, around the scratch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me guide your hand. Everyone reading by moonlight is relying on this cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three coffee rings on your farewell card. Circles again. The universe wants us together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm returning your keys. The moving van's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another ring! You're meant to stay in our circle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then help with this round table. It won't fit in the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A circle refusing to leave! The message is settled: this street must stay together. I'll set the table outside; bring the neighbours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said 'wait' as these station scales showed my weight. We're being told to stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're late. Our train's on platform four.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Four, and this ticket says 'for two.' The message concerns both of us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come on. It's going to Hope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course! Wait for hope. This journey is a test of faith; we're staying right here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss the kitchen fire, may I approve last week's minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The minutes are in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must establish whether anyone remembers them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember voting to replace the extinguisher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We can begin with matters arising.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wedding speeches go father, mother, best man, bride.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bride needs to say the groom hasn't arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That information belongs in her speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me to announce it now. The guests are leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Father introduces mother, mother introduces best man, best man introduces you as the bride's spokesperson. No anecdotes; we can get there in thirty seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As acting manager, I'm authorising everyone to stay late.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who appointed you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That question needs to be submitted on company stationery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You printed this stationery this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I've already established a proper channel for challenging it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm chairing this meeting under the emergency neighbourhood charter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are only two of us, and I haven't agreed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll record your objection before proceeding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Proceeding to what?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A vote to recognise my authority to record objections.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we sign off your evacuation plan, these arrows need the approved red.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone found the exit during the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll discuss that after the arrows match the sample.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sample faded in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a replacement sample before we can establish what everyone successfully followed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This cake cannot pass inspection. You've written 'Birthday Happy.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran out of room. Does it taste all right?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste is in section four. We need a correctly worded chocolate plaque over this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plaque will hide all the candles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then relocate them, keeping the count intact. We mustn't correct the greeting by falsifying your mother's age.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your family's dinners, that chair stays empty for your aunt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's abroad. Sit with us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only her grandchildren can borrow it. I learned that at Easter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then take mine. I'll fetch another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yours faces the kitchen; whoever sits there explains the dishes. Yes, I know them all now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At this club, 'interesting proposal' means withdraw it. I can help with the reply.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair said 'very interesting' and invited me to lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch is the exception. Keep the proposal; let them order first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come along. You can explain the menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the seating. Tell the secretary I'm your adviser; guests have to leave before coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring a sandwich to the permit office. I lost three Tuesdays learning that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says appointments take ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After they check your documents. Get that done at the side door; that was Tuesday two.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's marked staff only.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask reception to call the document clerk out. Don't follow the clerk back inside. Tuesday three was mostly explaining myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't ask the committee why the roof leaks. Ask which meeting owns the leak.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I asked why. They made me chair of causes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already asked me to investigate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for your predecessor's report. That's mine. It took six meetings to learn how to request a ladder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your moving van needs my release stamp. I'll help you get away promptly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The driver's charging by the minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you start loading. Send him in with the form; I'll handle everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's brought it. Can he go back to loading?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly, once I've stamped it. Meanwhile, he can help me find your file. Two of us should get you away faster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought the scissors for your club opening. I'll hand them over after the mayor's welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her speech is ten pages. Can you help her shorten it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll mark the sentence where I bring her the scissors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's skipping the speech. Just the ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll welcome everyone myself. She can hold the ribbon while I explain when I'll hand her the scissors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before dinner, we still split the first bread roll. Like when we shared a room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can afford two rolls now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll each have half of two.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's mathematically a whole roll.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but you can't buy the sharing separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You haven't given me our old knock before coming in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The key opens the door. The knock tells me it's you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can see me through the glass.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet I haven't heard from my best friend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I got your late job application accepted. You can take my Saturday shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was two years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've had the job for all of them. Saturday seems modest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It took you one phone call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make one to the manager. Tell her you're covering Saturday; we'll call that even.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Since I waived your joining fee, I'd like you to nominate me for treasurer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you back the fee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You repaid money. I made you an exception.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already nominated Ruth. She asked first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask her to nominate me. You can use your favor with her to settle yours with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's your visitor badge. The blue lift skips reception; lunch vouchers are inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks. Where's the toilet?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left of the lift. Take the badge; the door locks behind you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My colleague's holding it open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Give him this spare badge before you go in, or he'll need someone to hold it for him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Dad's dinner, bring bread even if he says not to. I'll explain the receipt business.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He texted me a shopping list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. 'Bread' means the crusty loaf; sliced makes him think you're staying for breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's attached a photograph of the loaf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll explain the acceptable substitutes before you reach the shop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My parking permit took six minutes at the expedited counter. Still filling yours in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finished in five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You must have found my counter. Did you mention the renewal exemption?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used the website. It applied that automatically.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you haven't learned where they hide the appeal button. I'll show you before you need it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You bowed twice at the awards dinner. The handbook specifies one bow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The host bowed back, so I returned it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you accidentally acknowledged them as senior.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They are the host.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I congratulated them without conceding rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you introduce me to the committee? Just not as your promising little discovery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How should I introduce you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As an independent professional whose work speaks for itself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you can introduce yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It speaks more clearly after you've said my name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please get me into the club, but don't tell them you rescued me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just signing your application.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A signature, not a creation story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It asks how I know you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the period after 'colleague' decisively.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're swapping your birthday-tea duty again? Last time you left me serving forty people alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This time Maya agreed to cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put her name on the rota. Mine appeared after you'd gone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write that you weren't responsible last time, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside the complaint about the cold tea, please. That's where everyone learned I was unreliable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're letting guests use the good mugs now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only because the other mugs are packed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I used one, you called it a breach of trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I replaced the mug. Will you tell them that when you do your usual warning about letting me carry things?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How did you get into the members' lounge without showing your pass?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They know me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll learn every doorman's birthday. Systematically.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can introduce you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, thank you. I'd like to develop spontaneous rapport properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found the right fork instantly. That's impressive. I've memorised this banquet's etiquette guide.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just copied our host. Watch me if you get stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you, but I'll identify each utensil independently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter needs your soup bowl. Shall I tell him you're finished?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, I'll arrange my spoon so he knows. Give me a moment to recall the angle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the complaint desk. We used to promise 'a person, not a number.' I still have my badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need my refund today. There's only a ticket machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take a number. Someone will call it. Someone always did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ticket says to post it away and wait six weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write 'a person, not a number' on the envelope. They may still recognise it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club always looks after its own. I've paid dues for thirty years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need your locker key. They've rented it to someone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There must be a respectful explanation. Could you check my thirty years?

beats.speaker: B
