beats.text: I did. They said I can give you a bag for your things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Could it have the club crest? We look after our own. I'm still... one of those.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This picnic form says 'bringing food.' I'm bringing plates. Will ticking it count as a wrong answer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tick it. I organise the picnic; I just need numbers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you initial it so they know you approved plates as food?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll add a plates box for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Could you mark the old box withdrawn so I don't fail to complete both?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The induction sheet says 'ask when appropriate.' May I check whether now is appropriate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I'm your trainer. What do you need?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you write 'questions permitted' beside this section? I don't want a warning on my first day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross that instruction out. Ask whenever you need.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you date the crossing-out? I've already asked under the old version.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written a checklist so you can safely make tea while I'm out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made tea for forty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You can initial the experience section.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just have water?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cold or room temperature? I need the correct appendix.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you borrow my bicycle, let's rehearse what to do if you wobble. I don't want you hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put my foot down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Which foot? I'll tick that side off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever side I'm falling toward. I need to get to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll practise both sides separately. Until both are signed off, you can borrow it for walking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first choir concert. I bowed when you did. Was that enough to count me in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Take another bow; they're still clapping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay down until you rise. I don't want to short-change the choir.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm staying down because my shoe's untied. Go and join the others.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll retie mine too. Then we can finish my first bows exactly together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first club dinner. I've learnt the toast so nobody regrets voting me in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stand and lift your glass with mine. We sit when the chair sits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same height as yours? I want to get this right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Any height. I have to sit; my knee's giving out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lean on me. I'll keep us both standing until the chair sits. I won't let my first toast fall short.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you thank me for the shed permit: that's an endorsement stamp, not an approval stamp.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Either way, the builders can start Monday. Thank you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday is commencement. Breaking ground is a separate term. Shall I explain?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Explain it to the builders. I need to order timber.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll prepare a glossary so they can appreciate exactly what I've obtained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you thank me for getting the leak fixed, it's a formal representation, not a complaint letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Your representation got us a plumber.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An emergency attendance. The regional salutation puts it in that category.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Help me file the receipt, then. What should I call the folder?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Emergency attendances, plural. Leave room for a note explaining how my salutation secured this one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Set an empty bowl for Great-Uncle Arthur before we serve dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Arthur is here this year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then he'll finally get to see his bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we put soup in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not after forty years of keeping it empty for him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we launch the boat, three circuits. Grandad always started at the bow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why three? The tide's right now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He did three every launch. Come round to the bow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already walked round twice carrying the ropes. Can those count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with ropes. Grandad collected those afterwards. Put them back and we'll begin properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The visitor book is missing your middle initial. Stop the tour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll add it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We need a witness for amendments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're watching me write.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who will confirm I was watching correctly?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You skipped item six on the kettle checklist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Item six says check that the lid is closed. It's closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But we can't prove you checked it before item seven.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll start again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First we need a procedure for interrupted kettle procedures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two hours for our stall permit. Imagine how thoroughly they're checking things.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The counter's empty. I need to get back to the shop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Nobody's being rushed into approving us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can apply online. It says there's a six-week review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. Let's join that queue from home. Six weeks of protection, and you can keep the shop open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our street-party application has reached a third committee. Reassuring to have so many safeguards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The first two lost it. I need to book the tables today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a third stands ready. One lost envelope can't plunge the street into chaos.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want a fresh application. The table company won't hold our booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good thing approval comes first. I'll reapply; you release the tables. Imagine seating everyone before we're protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's moon audit, who signs the village's findings?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The oldest owl. I'm delivering them, but my shift ends at sunset.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can we get its signature before you finish?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It starts at moonrise. I'll stay, but you have to approve my overtime.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved. Put 'waiting for owl' on your timesheet. Who covers delivery if it's cloudy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the dragon's naming ceremony, where do we put the fire extinguishers?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The dragon eats anyone who brings one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Who handles the insurance exemption?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody insures dragons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the deposit needs to cover the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This marriage certificate has the dot above the wrong letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've been married twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twenty years together. But until that dot moves, this doesn't certify a marriage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then move it. Our anniversary party starts at seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. But we'll need a wedding cake. This dot makes tonight our first day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your club resignation has the seal upside down. You're still our secretary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've moved abroad. Rotate the page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. Now your resignation is valid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. You can stop sending me the minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll rotate the previous eleven too. We may owe you a year's subscriptions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sat beside me at lunch. Shall I record that as our friendship policy?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was the only empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So friendship is allocated by availability. Useful clarification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow I'll save you a seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We've moved from allocation to a reserved entitlement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised before making tea. Is that our conflict-resolution procedure now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I knocked over your cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So material damage triggers refreshments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yesterday I made tea because you looked sad. Nothing broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sadness qualifies as damage. I'll amend the procedure before either of us has to smash anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won the bake-off, so next year's theme is cakes I already make.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You beat my lemon cake by half a point.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lemon cakes clearly get a fair chance under my leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll enter that same cake again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Returning challengers must improve by a full point. The champion sets the standard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As winner of family bowling, I choose where we eat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only agreed you'd get a trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A trophy recognises judgement under pressure. Mine says pizza.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brother can't eat cheese.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the next event is finding pizza he can eat. I'll award myself the biggest slice for organising it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That lost chess game was practice. This rematch will establish my reputation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've played here for thirty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I won't have thirty years remembered for one dropped rook.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just came for tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll make it. One excellent pot and you'll remember why you keep coming back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ignore my terrible karaoke score. The next song determines whether I still have it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody doubted you. It's just closing time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. One flawless song will keep it that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I unplugged it. I'm closing; your friends have gone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. One unaccompanied chorus will decide whether you book me for next Friday or forget my name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can't claim longest scarf until we've measured without stretching it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's obviously longer than yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind laying both flat against this tape.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours only reaches because of the tassels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quite right. Separate fringe measurements. I may have to surrender overall length and retain decorative reach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I certify your cake as tallest, does that sixty centimetres include the stand?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ten centimetres of stand. But I've already ordered the banner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the cake is fifty. The banner can't count the furniture.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put a ten-centimetre sponge underneath. Can you hold this end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. Then we'll measure again under its own weight. I'm not certifying the height of my hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you ask who invited me to the committee, I've balanced its accounts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still need a membership vote.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you circulate the accounts with my application? Especially the savings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't vote tonight. Nobody's taken the minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have. Alphabetised, with action points. Shall I read the section where you need a treasurer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've repaired the stage lights. Is there room for me in the theatre group now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just come to a rehearsal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll learn everyone's lines first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to audition for the audience.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll time my laughs so nobody loses a line. You'll want me in the front row.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely winning serve. My drills finally paid off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never trained with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You watched me practise. Observation is powerful teaching.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I copied the person who beat you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my defeat provided the lesson. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You negotiated a brilliant discount on that sofa. That's my influence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You told me to pay full price.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was provoking independent judgement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Next time I'll leave you at home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You're ready for unsupervised work. Ring me afterwards for your assessment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on winning the raffle. The prize is this hamper, once you've returned the basket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need the basket to carry everything home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow it until six. I'll keep the chocolates as a deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My bus doesn't get back until seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Seven is fine. I'll need the wine as well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've won the office parking space. I hold the allocation calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I park there tomorrow?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's a premium day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The prize said a free space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. We just haven't established when freedom applies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember our relay signal? Two taps meant you needed me to take over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're racing against each other today. I just want a fair start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said that before our county final. You needed a minute to breathe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My daughter thinks I'm nervous because she's watching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's missed the ankle bounce. That's your winning leg warming up. I've seen it bring us home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're giving me our old quiz-final look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're on different teams. I'm not asking for answers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Left eyebrow means you have two answers and hate both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My captain thinks I've got something in my eye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She hasn't sat through your geography rounds. I'll ask for another minute; you found Madagascar in the last one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I withdrew from last year's audition for you. I get first choice of songs now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to withdraw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I made the sacrifice easy to receive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thanked you. And I've already rehearsed the only song we both know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take that one. You can spend tonight learning something new; I spent last year letting you be heard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You had the good room on our last holiday. I'm choosing this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you liked the sofa bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was generous in both room allocation and commentary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The balcony room costs extra. I can pay the difference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. You cover the upgrade and I'll take the balcony. Last year's sofa bed can cover my share.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my queen where you can take it. Same as last Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to beat you properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can. I've also stopped practising so you can catch up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come back to chess club with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. But introduce me as your old coach. They only know me as the person you keep beating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've given you the good sales figures again. I'll explain the missing budget.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could split the difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You need a clean run at promotion. I can survive another meeting as the budget problem.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me introduce your section, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Say I'm explaining the hole, not that I dug it. Last time that distinction cost me a bonus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You beat me at darts yesterday, so you owe me lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. But you've just beaten me today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lunch cancels out. I owe you dessert for winning by more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it takeaway. I have to collect Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect her. A three-dart finish ought to cover a parent, not just a pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You won our tennis match, so you owe me first choice of film.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You won the rematch this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's your choice. Apparently I spent two hours earning your submarine documentary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three hours. It's a trilogy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll watch all three. But if you beat me tomorrow, you owe me the director's commentary on my musical.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't concede. Who else am I supposed to beat at chess on Tuesdays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've beaten me four times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Next game I start without my queen. Make me earn it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd still lose. Just take the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take both my rooks too. I'm not spending Tuesdays alone with something that can't gloat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't retire from the bake-off. Nobody else knows when my icing is smug.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm bored with sponge cakes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then wedding cakes. Three tiers each. Give me something to fear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I made those professionally for twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five tiers, then, and you choose the fillings. I'd rather lose sleep over you than win another sponge nobody insults properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we choose this year's holiday, settle who won the map argument in Cornwall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bridge was closed. Neither of us could test your shortcut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's reopened. Let's book the same cottage and time my route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll concede it's quicker. I want to go to Spain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me choose the airport route. Your concession needs one practical application.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set up our disputed chess position. Was my rook pinned or wasn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We came for dinner. I haven't played since we moved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll explain the position over starters. Then you can withdraw the cheating accusation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, you won. Pass the bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pass it when you say the move was legal. I can't defend my reputation with a dinner concession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sold every painting without looking busy. Book me the bigger room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Start with six. I'll help you hang them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve. Show me that relaxed lean you did beside the prices.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could relax because you handled all my sales.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sell my own twelve, glass in hand. You just keep me topped up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you finish five miles looking so relaxed? I'll do six smiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm exhausted. I just save my breath for the hill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll save enough to congratulate you at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can walk it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll jog ahead and find us a bench. You make recovery look easy; I could have it ready for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring back the old quiz questions. I won three years running with those.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all remember the answers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it would reward loyalty as well as knowledge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just want to win again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want the quiz to rediscover its standards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This old sales chart shows what I'm capable of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's from before we sold online.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's take the website down for a fair comparison.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put your phone number on the checkout page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put my photograph there too. In my best year people asked for me, not a basket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before announcing first place, could you say my name again with 'second'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Second is a wonderful result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use my name in that sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Congratulations, Alex. You came second.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Keep looking this way while they fetch the bigger trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put the winning photograph above mine. Can people still see mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is right beside the light switch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So everyone touches that wall. Good.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not a competition for attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody will mind if I stand beside it answering questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you teach the dog to fetch glasses, can I vote? I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my training experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And my experiment is making rent after the breakages.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include replacing the glasses in your definition of clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thirty people camping in our garden? I maintain that lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only one weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Followed by six Saturdays of reseeding. I want a say in tent placement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Put them wherever you like, but leave room for the fire pit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I need a say in that too. You've given me the seating plan for my next repair job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've fixed your gate. Shall I come next Sunday and do the gutter?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come for lunch. My brother's doing the gutter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll mend those dining chairs so there's room for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's already a chair for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll check the table legs. I'd like my place here to be something you can rely on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep me in the quiz team. I've learned every capital we missed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to justify coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll learn the currencies as a bonus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We like your company. Come early for a drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get there before you and reserve our table. You'll always have a seat if you keep mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you announce my cake won, mention I iced it at three in the morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ribbon says first prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ribbon got eight hours' sleep. It doesn't tell the full story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I mention the ingredients too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the ones I drove across town for after midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, we finished first. Please tell them whose weekend disappeared into that presentation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone worked hard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. My hard work includes a cancelled anniversary dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll thank your wife for lending us your weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank her for eating our anniversary dinner alone. If we're naming the team behind this win, she needs a place on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won our coin toss. Please announce who sits by the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do. Sit down; you're blocking the aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then announce my name from your seat. I'll approach when called.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The conductor needs to get past us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An official witness. Ask her to present the seat, and I'll accept it immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the next hand of cards, we need the winner's handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've won six hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And we've recognised only five. This is how records become unreliable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hand is tired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A nod will do if you make it ceremonial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose our picnic sandwich carefully. Pick badly and this is our last picnic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can share both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then both sandwiches get a chance to eliminate us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll taste them first. You can trust my choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now one bite decides whether I can ever trust you with lunch again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me choose Nina's birthday emoji. One wrong face and I'm out of her life.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Send a cake. That's what I sent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Matching cakes. She'll have to choose which friend to keep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell her we chose them together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're one entry. Before you send that, are you prepared for both of us never to see her again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last in the village quiz! Next week let's enter as a team of two.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We had six people and still lost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Imagine the comeback with four fewer brains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come if we study first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes! We'll study, then enter the county final. This defeat deserves a bigger audience.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cake collapsed. Next year I'll make one with three tiers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You couldn't manage one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. One tier is now my origin story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if three collapse?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then four will have an extraordinary burden of redemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely trophy. Who pays to insure it while it's in my house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The winner. We can display it here if you'd rather.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that transfer the insurance bill to the club?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. We'd ask you to polish it before open days.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many open days? I'd like to compare the insurance with the unpaid shifts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So winning best garden means I open it to visitors on Sunday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Our club keeps the admission money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who pays me for opening the gate and cleaning up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. But as winner, you join the committee that decides how we spend it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that committee meet here too? I need to know whether I've won a vote or another room to clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're not leaving the quiz until my missing half-point is restored.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We lost by thirty. I've booked dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move the booking. That half-point decides whether this evening was worth coming out for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The scorer can email a correction tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then book dinner tomorrow. I won't choose our celebration restaurant without the final half-point.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cake has one extra cherry. Put it in the winner's photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The flavour winner wasn't burnt. Yours was.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Photograph my extra cherry close up. That's the deciding advantage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then readers will want your recipe. Can I leave out the decorations?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave out anything except that cherry. I won't have readers following my winning recipe and ending up tied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You bought lunch again. You're building quite a lead in this friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You helped me move. I'm thanking you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've made my entire moving day worth one lunch. Excellent bargaining.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come to ours for Christmas. Nobody's keeping score.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're bringing the whole family into it. I'll bring breakfast for Boxing Day; this won't be decided over one turkey.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The neighbour returned my ladder cleaned. That's a move in the gardening rivalry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Perhaps it was just dirty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Now my ladder is cleaner than my windows.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could say thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concede the first round? Not before I've polished his wheelbarrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your garden party is approved for a small gathering. Go ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. I've invited fifty people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Small means everyone fits round our table. The approval stands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a bigger table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our table means the one we own. Tell the others their invitations are for another small gathering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may borrow the car for a short trip. That's settled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. I'll drive forty miles to the airport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short means the station at the end of our road. You're approved for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That works. I'll park there until I fly back next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short includes the car's stay. Return it before you catch the train. The permission stands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm chairing the club meeting until we locate the signed election result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have it. You lost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I respectfully propose we check both sides?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The back says the winner declined.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. My first decision is to store important documents face up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I hold the only key, so I decide when the rehearsal room opens.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine fits too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps you should choose today's schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's actually the cupboard key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You may schedule the cupboard. I'll handle the rehearsal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The engine is simple, apart from that red switch, which we'll leave alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to know what it does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First, understand the twelve systems surrounding it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They all point to the switch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A useful opportunity to revise all twelve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain every clause in this lease except the one about renewal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's why I brought it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should give it the benefit of a thorough introduction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just says 'automatically.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A deceptively advanced word. Let's revisit 'lease' first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put our gardening trophy in the old cupboard beside the piano.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We keep prizes on that shelf. We've never had a piano.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Open shelving. You've modernised since I organised the rose show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I founded this club last month. Tonight's our first meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fresh founding date too. Shall I give the new members some history before we put it all behind us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At our old reunions, Uncle Frank always carved the turkey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody here has an Uncle Frank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Families edit their history so quickly now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're at the wrong reunion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a remarkably efficient way to describe how much you've changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You spotted the deliberate error in my recipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You baked it that way yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A demonstration is more memorable than a warning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ate three slices.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Commitment to the lesson. I'm glad you're questioning authority now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've improved my filing system. Just the independence I hoped to provoke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your system lost every invoice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yours has found them. The learning journey is complete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did it by ignoring you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My most advanced outcome. I'll include it in the course description.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you explain why I shouldn't join the committee, shall I keep this envelope closed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me your reasons first. They sound carefully prepared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only admit people who contribute to the building.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps now is the moment for my receipt for its new roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go on explaining why you can't help me move. I'll save my little reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What reminder?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your reasons should have a fair chance without interference.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moving is something people should arrange themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely principle. Shall we apply it to the piano I moved for you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when you saved me the window seat? I thought I mattered to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I knew you liked the view.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Proof that you noticed small things.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Also, the seat beside it had less legroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So my fondest memory of being understood was your knees negotiating space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You kept my first terrible painting. That used to feel wonderfully loyal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still have it in the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you believed in me before anyone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It makes visitors appreciate your later work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ah. My earliest humiliation has become your introduction to the house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fixed my bike, so I owe you dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was repaying the dinner you cooked last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your repair was too good. I owe you for the surplus kindness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't cook again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're saving me work. The debt has increased.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel's upstairs. We're even for yesterday's lift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's yours. I brought it in from the rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I owe you twice. I'll take your rubbish down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three flights with a leaking bag? That clears both debts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leaking? That puts you in debt. You can repay me by cleaning the stairs behind me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tap's leaking again. Give me the spanner before you start pricing lifeboats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've found the valve. You look terrified.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you fix it. I'll keep the towels ready for when the kitchen goes under.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The valve's stuck. What if I snap it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the spanner. You take the towels; you've reached the sinking-kitchen stage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The projector's dead. Usually I talk you down, but today I need you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can use my laptop. Nobody's going to die.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep saying that while I imagine twelve directors sharing one screen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My laptop's dead too. We're finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's going to die. I'll print twelve copies; you sit down before we need thirteen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cake won because it was minimalist. I'm removing half my decorations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won for giving everyone a slice. Yours stayed behind glass.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll serve pieces twice your size. Pass me the knife.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a queue of twenty. I cut mine small so nobody missed out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine will be thinner. I'll feed the queue and the people they go home to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got the supplier's price down by staying calm. I'll be quieter on our next call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You shouted through this one. I need you to let me finish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll leave longer pauses than you. We'll see whose silence saves more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I got the discount by asking about damaged boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll ask about every dent. You can handle the quiet part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my spare key. I trust you completely these days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just make a tiny adjustment to your shelves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give the key back. 'Tiny adjustment' preceded the last collapse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't touch a shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The key is yours until 'improvement' enters the conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're in charge of my birthday. I know you'll keep it simple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just a small surprise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That phrase cost me a weekend in a mascot suit last year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No costume this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can keep planning. Slowly, and without using 'surprise' again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can give you another concert ticket. That doesn't mean we're past that evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was outside the door the whole time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it wasn't distance. You were that close and left me alone with it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I heard you say my name. I thought you wanted me to stay out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then what I carried as silence was you listening. I don't know how to hand you this ticket now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me answer this letter. I still can't read your handwriting without going back to that afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote it before you arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it wasn't something I said. You'd already decided.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I left the envelope open because I hoped you'd stop me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So what I thought was your decision was a test I didn't know I was taking. Sit with me while I answer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called my cake impressive. I'll add a second tier before you leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The icing is perfect already. I came for a slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Then the second tier needs icing roses. Perfect can't just happen twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You make those beautifully. Could mine go in a box? My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll make your rose climb the lid. You should leave with something better than beautiful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said I handled the meeting well. I'll improve tomorrow's agenda before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your summary was excellent. Come get a sandwich with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I'll make tomorrow's half as long, with clearer decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're brilliant at making things simple. Explain the budget to me over lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. If simple is my standard, I'll get the whole budget onto your napkin before the sandwiches arrive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My teenage self would hate me buying this sensible car.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It has excellent insurance rates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly the sort of sentence he swore never to say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then buy the motorbike.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Let him be disappointed somewhere with airbags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I promised my younger self I'd never leave this town.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You also wanted to live on the moon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Some ambitions were symbolic. Loyalty wasn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So you're staying?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I'm taking the photograph so he can disapprove from a better view.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our restaurant passed inspection? Even the grease trap?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Spotless. I had it pumped out. Can I start cooking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So the trouble's moved into the tanker. Is it still outside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sealed. Nothing can escape.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we've bottled it under pressure beside our diners. Ask the driver to leave before I unlock the doors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The neighbours liked my speech? I thought they'd vote me off the committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've asked you to chair next month's meeting. Please say yes; I'm exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they're keeping me where they can watch me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit beside you and handle complaints.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've given me a minder. Will you be reporting my mistakes to them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix your bike before you ride. I know which bolts matter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've tightened them already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll check the checking. There must be something left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just come riding with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Without a repair to do? Give me a minute to remember how.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me your landlord's number. I'll get your deposit back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Already done, Mum. I'm taking you out to celebrate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me book. You still need someone who checks the reviews.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked your favourite. Just bring yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not even a cake? Could you forget your reading glasses? I could read you the menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought this jacket for my first supper at your sailing club. Will I fit in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're casual. Roll your sleeves up; I'll introduce you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. I'm one of those relaxed old hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lovely. I'll tell them you're new so they'll explain things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I'm returning. You can explain the boats privately. These sleeves suggest I already know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wanted a more adventurous friend, so I've booked us climbing lessons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant trying a new cafe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well, I'm a climbing person now. I've told my sister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cancel. I need a friend who listens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm a listener. Will you tell my sister I listened to you, rather than gave up climbing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the hall minutes, just say the roof's repaired. My six weekends aren't worth recording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. I'm keeping the minutes to one page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These dated invoices can go separately. My initials only show who paid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put them in the accounts folder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. A tiny footnote will do: accounts, pages one to forty. No need to name me twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Anyone could have organised the concert. My thirty-seven calls were hardly heroic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thirty-seven?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the completed ones. I wouldn't inflate the figure with attempts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want a thank-you speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, no. Just make sure whoever writes it has the call log.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait, don't drink yet. Two taps on the cup first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: For luck? That's good tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps meant Mum had made it weak. We'd better tap again; she'll think we've gone polite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I miss her complaints. The table's too quiet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two more, then. These are to leave her a turn. We can wait before we drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your audition, knock twice on this door. We can't skip that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They knocked back. Can we go in? My hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twice again. Now we're saying we're ready, even if your hands aren't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're calling me in alone. How will I know you're still here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll knock twice when your song ends. This time it means I'm staying until you come out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That little crack beside the piano was the stage warning us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The piano's leaning. Help me move it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The crack's opened a place for the whole piano. Keep your end away from it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The front row's tilting too. I'm clearing the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's reached the audience. That little crack is taking the whole concert downstairs. I'll get the balcony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They misspelled our wedding invitation. That was the warning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake names another couple. Help me scrape it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same mistake, larger icing budget. Pass me a knife.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They booked that couple into our reception room too. We've both paid; I'm offering half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The typo's taking half our wedding. Before you offer them my chair, check which name's on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, our outdoor concert is sold out!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just been cancelled for rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, we've created an unforgettable sense of demand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're refunding everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And demonstrated generosity at full capacity. Exactly the evening I hoped for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've been chosen to run the chess club tournament! Finally, I can shape the whole day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They changed their minds. You're on refreshments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful! Running it was a triumph; now I get the personal contact I wanted too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a self-service urn. I only need you to refill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect! Leadership, hospitality, and now uninterrupted time to study chess. Every appointment has been inspired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our garden fountain grants wishes. Fine. We're still paying for its water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wished for ten more. We can sell admission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eleven fountains on our meter. Charge enough to cover that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Visitors wished for fountains at home. They're all fed from ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're paying to water the whole queue's gardens. Sell them monthly passes before the next bill arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, our house travels through time. Can we stop somewhere that fixes roof tiles?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ancient Rome. I'll find a roofer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Get a quote. The bucket's already half full.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I touched the dial. We're underwater now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. That same leak is admitting the sea. Reverse us while I empty the bucket into the sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave you that key because you were welcome here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then why are you holding it like evidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the cupboard was locked before the cake disappeared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I brought you a replacement cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps the key is a subscription. We'll discuss the terms over tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep this old ticket. It proves we went somewhere together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It proves you booked us different trains.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's evidence of a mistake we survived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I kept my ticket too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put them together. Now they're an invitation to get it right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make yourself at home. I've put fresh coffee on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've brought six suitcases.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make yourself at home? I thought you meant a weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just until my flat is repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make yourself at home. I'll clear the drawer, but we're counting weekends together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Anything for you.' That's what I said when you asked for a lift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now could we collect my piano?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Anything for you was much lighter five minutes ago.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the piano you learned on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Anything for you. But you're carrying the end with the memories.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That flat-pack cupboard's leaning. I could take a look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold it for a second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought a blanket. Your heater's still broken?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm managing. Leave the blanket, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. Would you say you needed my help?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need the blanket. I can reset the heater myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The fuse box is in my locked cupboard. Shall I wait while you manage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you get your train, could you taste this soup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you zip your suitcase, let me wrap that jar of jam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your train jumper. We'll need to unpack it and find something else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the jam here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you haven't tasted it. I'll get a spoon before you decide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'd like to be able to smile at you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we'd sorted this out by text.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sent a thumbs-up. I couldn't hear any remorse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a sad face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right here. Could you give the sad face a sentence beginning with 'I'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you support a small improvement to the front garden?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What sort of improvement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something with a pond. And no tree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where's the tree?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So standing guests would be more considerate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six. I've already invited them. Would borrowing enough chairs for everyone turn that into a yes?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These eighty wedding place cards need names. Your bin labels have better lettering than our invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd read the names. You'd only do the beautiful part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle my aunt. The ink colour could be entirely yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you say you heard about the party, which part?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gave you the timing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have you watched it, or are we both relying on my brother?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What did the manager say about the missing keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They might be in the drain. You locked up, didn't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is she asking everyone who locked up, or just me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just you. Someone saw you outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did they say what I was doing, or only where I was?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you keep Mum in the kitchen while I hide her birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you stop telling her I'm the one who plans these things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This one's mine. Could you ask her to show you her pastry trick?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll peel the apples tonight. Could you get us twenty minutes and a pie?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you help me set up Denise's surprise leaving party at seven?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent the last one washing glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wash up. Could you get Denise out of the office while I decorate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She won't leave before I finish her spreadsheet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send it over. I'll finish her spreadsheet; could you take her for coffee and complain about how little I do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your rooftop wedding photo would look lovely. Try that staff-only door first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'll forgive you. I'll follow once you've explained the dress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then carry my train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll hold the very end, so if they object, only your train has followed you in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try a grape before we buy the bunch. Last week's were sour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just one. I'll try the next if nobody objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, but you're holding the bunch where the assistant can see you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll hold it out like samples. You take the first one; if that works, I'll serve myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole town's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who stopped it leaning into the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've thanked the wedding guests. What about the person who cooked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make an announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead of the concert. I've made your favourite cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring your concert friend too. I'll reimburse both tickets in cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only went because I promised her dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clear the living room. You can choose the music; I'd just like to be in the room with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take me as your expedition photographer instead of Martin. I speak French.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're crossing a desert, not interviewing people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sponsor's French. I could send them updates they can actually use.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want their logo visible in every picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it on the water flask. Martin photographs untouched wilderness; I'll make sure yours looks generously funded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office plant's dead. I'll interview everyone who watered it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent lead. I'll test the machine. It may be dispensing something harmful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made that coffee yourself. With six sugars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll prepare six-sugar samples for comparison. We may be dealing with a plant that couldn't handle hospitality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open that rent letter yet. Help me hang our new curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He'll love how we're looking after the place. Let's get a photo of the curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send him one and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet showing. Let's rearrange the room first. You move the sofa; I'll hold your phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I answer about the office kitchen, what happened to the printer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Paper jam. Now, why is there smoke?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did you cause the jam? I need that cleared up first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used sticky labels. Can we talk about the smoke now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they the labels marked 'not for printers'? Let's finish your statement before starting mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we plan Mum's apology dinner, why did she spend her birthday outside the restaurant?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did you forget, or assume I'd book it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Give me that bit, then you get the present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've advanced the charity our estimated auction takings. Now we just need bidders.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You borrowed five thousand. Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One bidder keeps catering costs down. That's responsible fundraising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must bid ourselves. Raise the card limit; protecting that donation has to come first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get your boiler running. I know these controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll need someone on the boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asks what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're still establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions so he can concentrate on readings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Excellent chance for a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a free shower!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brilliant. The shower's finally reached your feet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. Stay there; I'll get a cloth. We can fix this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep blotting. You're doing well. That carpet was my birthday present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's spreading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. Good catch. Take my clean shirt. I am absolutely furious, but you are not tackling this alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the birthday lunch you really want. I'll drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds wasted. Fine. You love the sea; let's make a day of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another forty? Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. Give me the number. You're getting your sea view. Ask for a window; you deserve one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One lift, then. And tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds. Three if you say we're still friends when you hand it over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if I get first choice of Christmas dates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already expects me Christmas Day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Boxing Day, then. In exchange, I'll tell her I'm no longer hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather you actually stopped being hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay through New Year and I'll mean it. I'll even stop mentioning the birthday to Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help you move the sofa. I'll take the cushions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're sewn on. We have to lift together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You lift; I'll say when. Together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need another person underneath it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll book someone on your phone. Then I can give both of you the same countdown.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll look after your dog during the kitchen repairs. Bring him over after his walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Stay in my guest room; you can handle breakfast while I sleep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can stay, but his six o'clock walk is your job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll organise it: lead by the door, your alarm at five thirty. You won't have to plan a thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two office biscuits are missing. We've got an organised operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A confession this quick suggests training.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they're recruiting through hunger. This goes higher than the biscuit tin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody received my meeting email. This office has stopped communicating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You forgot to send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And nobody noticed. Our entire communication system depends on my memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it. Go and have your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're covering communications while I'm absent. We need a succession plan before I take a sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold this shelf bracket against the holes? It keeps slipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you turn that top screw once? Then you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are already lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tighten those, then? And slide the shelf onto it to check. I'll get your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, could you check this window latch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's shut. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why's the curtain moving?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The fan's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you show me which switch? There are several.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One last cup to dry before your taxi arrives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you reach the shelf for it? I'll fetch your coat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's away. The driver's calling; I really have to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you put him on speaker first? I should thank him for waiting. What's his name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my wet sock beside your dinner. From your puddle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind it sharing the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you move it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An apology would dry the atmosphere considerably.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the bus timetable. I circled every bus I missed waiting for you to return my keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three circles. And here's the takeaway receipt from when my dinner was still hot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy another dinner. Can we put the papers away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. Say you're sorry, and we can clear the table instead of reconstructing my evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quick yes to the garden party before the booking expires?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's secure the date, then count chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And the cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the quote while you say yes. That way we won't lose the booking while you're reading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just nod and I'll accept the sofa delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will it fit through the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can measure after securing the bargain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nod before they start measuring too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name's beside bathroom duty. Here's the mop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is your training opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you show me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. First, accept the mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took your bins out once during your holiday. I didn't volunteer for life. Tonight's yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours already send you the reminders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce you in the group as their permanent bin contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in it until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay until you send 'I'll handle Thursday.' They can welcome you while I leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did we settle on for Mum's birthday dinner? I'm checking the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, in the private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. How have you written the restaurant name? I want everything consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't written anything. You're doing the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then could you proofread the booking confirmation aloud? I'll type straight from you so we don't introduce any errors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's hike: ridge or river? I'm checking the weather against our route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flood warning, then. Where are we meeting? I'll add that to the reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me that twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Brief me like a new recruit; I'll take notes, starting with where I report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the manager we agreed I'd cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you have no conflicting memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not lying for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Turn the kitchen tap on before I start washing up. I've tightened the loose joint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear my apron. I need to know whether the joint holds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it and turn the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll need it dry for washing up. You can have my raincoat for the test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still have proper coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you like this, we can save the proper stuff for guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not sacrificing breakfast to save you money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sip. If it's awful, I'll buy you a croissant and keep my cup empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you call that a quick shop, I carried twelve bags up six flights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. The frozen peas came up separately. That was a second trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you sit down twice. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
